A significant microbial community shift towards known potential oil degraders such as Alphaproteobacteria, Melainabacteria, Gammaproteobacteria, Deltaproteobacteria, Spirochaetia and/or Acidobacteriia was observed, indicating their potential role in oil degradation and resilience despite the toxicity caused by the oil/associated metals. QPCR analysis indicated an increased presence of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon ring hydroxylating dioxygenase genes (PAH-RHDαGN), confirming the existence of potential PAH-degrading microorganisms. This suggests that targeted PCR analyses could be used to assess the oil contamination extent and evaluate the bioremediation potential of impacted environments. It underscores the importance of a comprehensive indigenous microbial community assessment including their in situ hydrocarbon degradation potential. Comparative microcosms analysis demonstrated that dynamic responses of these communities across environmental settings provide a valuable insight into natural attenuation processes occurring in oil-contaminated soils. Combined, these approaches provide a framework for assessing microbial-driven oil degradation and a guide to develop effective/sustainable bioremediation strategies.

title: Rhodamine B degradation through sulfite activation by Vernadite: Kinetics characteristics and reaction mechanism
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Wenteng Chu, Runshen Feng, Cheng Wang, Yanting Pan, Hong Su, Feng Jiang, Xiaoming Wang, Hui Yin, Xionghan Feng
abstract: Vernadite is often used for pollutant adsorption, oxidation and interfacial catalysis due to its diverse structure, high reactivity and environmental friendliness. Rhodamine B was employed as a model organic contaminant in this study to investigate the capability of Vernadite-activated sulfite for organic pollutant degradation and to elucidate the activation mechanism of sulfite in the Vernadite/sulfite system. Vernadite was able to partially decolorize approximately 90.3% of Rhodamine B (RhB) due to its strong surface activity. Upon the addition of sulfite, RhB was fully degraded within 20 min, and the solution was observed to change from red to colorless. It was discovered that dissolved oxygen was crucial to the process. As the sulfite content rose, the degradation efficiency first rose and then decreased, but it rose as the mineral dosage increased. The system was effective within the pH range of 3-7, though efficiency declined as pH increased. The presence of common coexisting ions had minimal impact on the performance, particularly in the presence of humic acid (HA), where degradation remained effective. Mn (III) and singlet oxygen (1O2) were confirmed to be the primary reactive species in charge of RhB degradation by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and quenching studies. These results demonstrate the possible uses of minerals containing manganese dioxide as heterogeneous catalysts for environmental remediation under realistic wastewater treatment conditions.

title: A novel zirconium oxide gel-based method for measuring phosphate oxygen isotopes in different soil phosphorus pools
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Baoying Wang, Yu Sun, Zhao Wei
abstract: Phosphorus (P) limitation in soils is a prevalent issue across diverse ecosystems, underscoring the need for a comprehensive understanding of soil P sources and transformation pathways to improve P utilization efficiency. The phosphate oxygen isotope composition (δ18OP) of different pools of phosphate (PO4 3−) is an effective tool for characterizing soil P cycling processes. However, a lack of comparable purification methods for different PO4 3− pools remains. Here, we established a pretreatment method based on Zirconium oxide gels (ZrO-gels) for purification δ18OP analysis of different PO4 3− pools. This study used three soil types: Oxisols, Mollisols, and Alfisols. Pretreatment involved combining ZrO-gels adsorption, CePO4 precipitation, and Ag3PO4 precipitation to purify NaHCO3–P, NaOH–P, and HCl–P pools. The PO4 3− recovery ratio across all purification steps ranged from 86.1% to 92.8%. SEM-EDS analysis confirmed the high purity of Ag3PO4. The atomic Ag:P ratios for samples derived from the NaHCO3–P (Ag:P = 3.8 ± 0.1), NaOH–P (Ag:P = 3.7 ± 0.2), and HCl–P (Ag:P = 3.7 ± 0.3) were in close agreement with the theoretical Ag:P ratio of pure Ag3PO4 (Ag:P = 3.5). For all soil types, the δ18OP values consistently followed the pattern: NaHCO3–P > NaOH–P > HCl–P, which reflects biological turnover periods and geochemical constraints of different P pools. This study confirms that the ZrO-gels-based method is effective for δ18OP pretreatment across diverse soil types. This method addresses the lack of standardization, thus providing a convenient method for tracing soil P cycling.

title: Methane production dynamics in fluid fine tailings of an oil sand pit lake
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Chenlu Wang, Han Bao, Greg F. Slater
abstract: The reclamation of oil sands mining sites is a regulatory requirement for oil sands mine operators, ensuring the restoration of post-mining landscapes to locally common, functional ecosystems. Water-capped tailings technology (WCTT), which involves placing a layer of water over tailings deposited in a mined-out pit to create a pit lake. This is a tailings reclamation concept being tested. The Base Mine Lake Demonstration (BML), commissioned by Syncrude Canada Ltd in 2012, serves as the first full-scale demonstration of water-capped tailings technology. Microbial methane production in fluid fine tailings (FFT) influences BML development because aerobic methane oxidation in the water column can deplete oxygen levels, methane ebullition transports organic compounds from FFT to the water column, and methane emission from the lake is a source of greenhouse gas. This study investigated methane production dynamics in BML by measuring methane concentrations, stable carbon isotope composition (δ13C), and methane production rates across five sampling locations. Dissolved methane concentrations showed consistency with previous years. Methane production rates in BML FFT ranged from 1 to 28 μmol/L FFT/day, comparable to rates observed for petroleum hydrocarbon-derived microbial methane production. Methane production rates exhibit spatial variability across depths and locations and were strongly correlated with naphtha content, suggesting that the low molecular weight hydrocarbons in naphtha serve as a primary carbon source for microbial methanogenesis in FFT. These findings on methane production dynamics have direct implications for understanding the BML development and optimizing oil sands reclamation strategies.

title: High-pressure adsorption of CO 2 on montmorillonite
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Kun Luo, Hang Wang, Dong Liu, Zhiqiang Yu, Ping'an Peng
abstract: Geological Carbon Sequestration (GCS), a pivotal technology for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions through the capture and long-term storage of carbon dioxide (CO2) in underground geological formations, plays a crucial role in combating climate change. Montmorillonite, a widely distributed mineral in storage formations, exhibits significant potential for GCS due to its high specific surface area and CO2 adsorption capacity. However, the adsorption mechanisms of CO2 in montmorillonite under reservoir conditions remain insufficiently characterized, particularly concerning two critical aspects: (1) the dynamic diffusion process regulating CO2 intercalation into interlayer space, and (2) the distinct adsorption behaviors—including both adsorption capacity disparity and binding energy differentiation—between external surfaces and interlayer space. This study conducted laboratory simulations of CO2 adsorption experiments using natural montmorillonite and heat-treated montmorillonite (calcined at 600 °C to close the interlayer space) at 25 °C, 50 °C, and 75 °C. The results revealed that the adsorption capacity within the interlayer space exhibits a positive correlation with increasing pressure. CO2 molecules entered the interlayer space substantially at pressures ≥14 bar and the adsorption capacity can even reach 62.7% (75 °C) of the total adsorption capacity at 50 bar. These findings highlight the critical role of interlayer space of montmorillonite in CO2 adsorption in geological CO2 storage formations, offering new insights into montmorillonite CO2 adsorption mechanism.

title: Global biogenic isoprene emissions modulated by intensifying warm temperature extremes
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Matthews Nyasulu, Adharsh Rajasekar, Emmanuel Yeboah, Genesis Magara
abstract: Biogenic isoprene, the most abundant non-methane volatile organic compound, plays a critical role in air quality and climate. While its emissions are known to be temperature-dependent, the specific causal link to the intensification of warm temperature extremes observed in recent decades remains understudied. This study provides causal evidence connecting the rising intensity of warm temperature extremes to trends in biogenic isoprene emissions from 2000 to 2019. We integrated high-resolution CAMS-GLOB-BIOv3.1 emission data with ERA5 reanalysis products and applied the Information Flow (IF) framework to quantify the causal influence of extreme temperature on isoprene emission trends. Our results reveal a significant increase in isoprene emissions (>1.2 Tg yr−1) in tropical hotspots, which were significantly correlated with the intensity of extreme temperature (r > 0.8, p < 0.05). Importantly, causal analysis quantified a persistent, unidirectional IF from extreme temperatures to isoprene emissions, while the reverse pathway was negligible. This establishes extreme temperature as among the drivers of rising biogenic isoprene emissions, revealing a critical positive climate feedback loop under warming climate extremes. These findings highlight the need to incorporate extreme temperature–driven biogenic isoprene emission feedbacks into climate and air quality models to improve atmospheric composition and inform effective mitigation strategies for public health and climate stability.

title: Metal contaminant availability in freshly dredged sediments and controlling reactive mineral and organic surfaces
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Maarten C.J.M. Van Hoef, Joris J. Dijkstra, Rob N.J. Comans
abstract: In this paper we evaluate the environmental and geochemical properties of freshly dewatered dredged sediment at the start of a multiyear field-scale ripening experiment designed to obtain suitable material for construction. The solid-solution partitioning of metal(loid) contaminants was determined over a wide pH-range and related to the binding properties of natural reactive mineral and organic surfaces in the sediment. The results were interpreted using a multisurface geochemical model, comparing partitioning with the ‘generalised two layer model’ (GTLM) and ‘charge distribution and multisite ion complexation’ (CD-MUSIC) submodels, which differ in the level of detail for adsorption of major and minor ions to Fe- and Al-(hydr)oxides. The measured and modelled solubility of metal(loid)s varied by several orders of magnitude across the pH-range, often with a minimum around neutral pH. Surface characterisation showed a high reactive surface area for the metal (hydr)oxides and a low organic matter reactivity for metal binding, in contrast to terrestrial soils. Consequently, the adsorption to metal (hydr)oxides was dominant in the modelled speciation of several metal(loid) contaminants. Despite this importance of metal (hydr)oxides, only minor differences were found between the solid-solution partitioning predicted using the GTLM and the CD-MUSIC submodels. Therefore, the predicted solid-solution partitioning did not fully reflect the benefits offered by the more mechanistic CD-MUSIC model for contaminant adsorption to metal (hydr)oxides in the sediment. We conclude it is rather the conceptual framework of the CD-MUSIC model which, when combined with independent information from surface characterisation and pH-dependent extractions, contributes to understanding contaminant behaviour in the freshly dredged sediment.

title: Modelling of geochemical survey data via self-supervised graph learning and distance-encoding Transformer
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 204 Author(s): Zhiyi Chen, Yihui Xiong, Yao Fan, Renguang Zuo
abstract: The recognition of geochemical anomalies is crucial for mineral resource assessments. However, developing effective models to capture the intricate spatial patterns in geochemical survey data, as well as overcoming the limitations posed by the scarcity of training samples, remain two significant hurdles in the application of deep learning algorithms to modelling geochemical survey data. In this study, we propose a framework combining self-supervised graph learning and Transformer to recognize geochemical anomalies related to mineralization. The framework employs graph convolutional networks to capture local spatial features in geochemical survey data, while the Transformer is introduced to model global spatial dependencies, addressing the limitations of graph neural networks in handling global spatial information. We construct a geochemical graph based on distance thresholds and cosine similarity between graph nodes. Additionally, a distance encoding mechanism is designed to assist the Transformer in capturing the topological structure of the geochemical graph, enabling precise modelling of both local spatial correlations and global connectivity. The effectiveness of the model in recognizing geochemical anomalies is validated in the southern Tianshan region of China, with the integration of Transformer significantly improving its ability to capture global connectivity and enhance the performance of anomaly recognition in complex geological environments. Moreover, the inclusion of the distance encoding mechanism further enhances model performance, improving its ability to recognize geochemical anomalies. This method has demonstrated its effectiveness in capturing complex anomaly patterns, delivering crucial geochemical insights that may support forthcoming mineral prospecting activities in the region.

title: Unveiling metal deposition and source apportionment in sediments of Daya Bay (China) through multiple radionuclide tracing and analytical modelling
description: Publication date: Available online 20 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Yufei Gao, Qianqian Wang, Zhaoxi Liu, Wei Wang, Tianwei Wang, Chong Sheng, Hailong Li
abstract: Coastal sediments play an important role in metal cycling processes in the ocean. However, systematic investigations integrating metal deposition processes, source identification, and quantitative assessments in coastal surface sediments remain limited. Here, we combined multi-radionuclide (228Th, 228Ra/226Ra, and 210Pb) tracing techniques to quantify the sediment accumulation rate (SAR) and metal burial fluxes in Daya Bay, China. Metal sources and their contributions were further assessed using self-organizing map (SOM) and positive matrix factorization (PMF) models. The estimated average SAR was 1.29 cm yr-1. The mean burial fluxes of metals followed the order: Cd < Cu < Cr < Pb < As < Ni < Zn < Ba < Mn, with values ranging from 0.06 to 443.01 μg cm-2 yr-1. Source apportionment analysis by SOM and PMF models revealed that metal inputs originated from industrial activities (34.9%), agricultural and aquacultural activities (29.2%), transportation and domestic activities (20.1%), and mixed sources of natural processes and human activities (15.8%). Overall, anthropogenic activities were identified as the dominant contributors to metal pollution. This study revealed that multi-radionuclide tracing techniques facilitated reconstructing the sedimentary dynamics and pollution histories, highlighting the substantial influence of anthropogenic activities on metal pollution in coastal zones.

title: A Simple, Field-Compatible Method for Accurate pH Measurement in Hypersaline Brines
description: Publication date: Available online 18 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Paz Nativ, Gordon D.Z. Williams, Avner Vengosh
abstract: Accurate pH determination in hypersaline brines is essential for reliable geochemical modeling and simulation, particularly for processes such as direct lithium extraction, carbonate precipitation potential calculations, brine reinjection assessments, and related applications. However, standard pH electrode calibration techniques may produce significant errors in concentrated brines due to elevated liquid junction potential (LJP) and ion interactions with the electrode’s glass membrane. Here, we present a robust, field-compatible method for accurate pH measurement in high salinity brines, using standard combined glass pH electrodes and titration-based calibration with tailored buffer solutions. The technique integrates an online PHREEQC (Pitzer model) based software to prepare custom buffer solutions and calibration curves, enabling the re-analysis of field data for correct pH detection. The method was evaluated using data from 16 hypersaline brines across the full evaporation sequence of a lithium production plant in the Salar de Uyuni of Bolivia. pH values obtained using the new method resulted in substantially improved agreement between PHREEQC-simulated and measured total alkalinity compared to standard pH calibration. While simulations based on standard pH calibration showed increased scatter and large errors with increasing ionic strength (up to >95% in total alkalinity simulations), applying the new method reduces these errors to within ±10% across the entire salinity range. This approach provides a simple, generic, low-cost, and effective tool for improving the pH measurement and chemical characterization of hypersaline brine.

title: Carbonate Associated Sulphate (CAS) in travertines: A useful time capsule for inferring (paleo-) fluid-rock interaction and/or microbial fractionation?
description: Publication date: 20 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 716 Author(s): Hannes Claes, Guillaume Paris, Rudy Swennen
abstract: In light of continental sulphur cycling, we verified whether Carbonate Associated Sulphate (CAS) in travertines preserves pristine fluid signatures and can be used in geothermal exploration or as dating or stratigraphic tool, similarly to δ34S measured in marine carbonates. In other words, can CAS be applied to infer sulphur source in travertines, or is it affected by microbial mediation and/or diagenesis? Therefore, novel CAS analyses from travertines of famous deposits from Turkey (Ballık), Italy (Tivoli) and Hungary (Budakalász and Süttő) were evaluated within their hydrogeological context. Results show that travertines dominantly inherited CAS and δ34S from their spring waters, controlled by paleo-geo-hydrology. The CAS signature consequently helps to pinpoint source rocks, providing complementary information to elemental compositions, O, C and Sr isotopes. Of potential interest for geothermal exploration, the studied cases reveal a “Travertine Play”, i.e. different factors sharing similar exploration goals, of 1) elevated geothermal gradients, 2) active tectonics and presence of large-scale fault systems, 3) topography for gravity driven fluid flow and 4) (evaporite-bearing) carbonates in the subsurface as “ingredients” for travertine formation. Sulphur in travertines, as reflected by δ34S, originated respectively from the Late Triassic Kaleboğazi Formation (Ballık area), the Late Triassic Burano Formation (Tivoli area) and the Triassic (-Permian) evaporites mixed with leaching from Oligocene sulphides (Budakalász and Süttő areas). Microbial fractionation and diagenesis only play a minor role. The δ34S signature of travertines along their stratigraphy, consequently, provides an exquisite record of subsurface fluid-rock interaction and evolution through time. In this way, Pleistocene interplay between paleo-tectonics and -climate remains “set in travertine stone”.

title: Estimation of the association constants of rare earth elements in aqueous solutions in STP conditions ( t = 25 ° C , P = 1 b a r ) from their electronegativities and polarizabilities
description: Publication date: 20 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 716 Author(s): Imed Eddine Nezli, Guilhem Bourrié
abstract: Rare earth elements associate with ligands in aqueous solutions. A model correlating association constants with electronegativities and polarizabilities of REE is proposed. Variation of coordination number from light REE (LREE) to heavy REE (HREE) is taken into account. The model applies to all elements from lanthanum ( Z = 57 ) to lutetium ( Z = 71 ), in the trivalent state. However to improve the model, rare earth elements (REE) were divided into two subsets, both including LREE and HREE: one consists of REE that present in some of their oxidation states a 4 f subshell either zero, half filled f 7 or full f 14 , namely La, Ce, Eu, Gd, Tb, Yb and Lu, i.e. elements ”inside the central block” defined by Laing (2009); the other consists of REE that do not access to oxidation states with a 4 f subshell either zero, half filled f 7 or full f 14 , namely Pr, Nd, Pm, Sm, Dy, Ho, Er and Tm, i.e. ”outside the central block”. They are designed hereafter respectively as ICBREE (inside the central block REE) and OCBREE (outside the central block REE). Double linear regressions of association constants with electronegativities and polarizabilities were obtained separately on each subset or globally. Better fits were obtained separately. Association constants ( log K ) were then estimated to ± 0.03 to 0.1 logarithmic unit. Standard deviation of residuals is smaller in the OCBREE (“simple” REE) subset than in the ICBREE (more complex REE) subset. Sulfate association constants decrease while phosphate association constants increase from LREE to HREE. Chloride and nitrate association constants are independent on the specific REE. Association constants with Image 1001 , Image 1002 and Image 1003 slightly increase from LREE to HREE. The ratio sulfate/phosphate may thus fractionate REE in waters, soils and sediments. The new set of association constants is incorporated in a modified version of wateqfREYsKinetics.dat database.

title: Coupled crystallisation and chaotic mixing of basaltic and dacitic magmas under sub-liquidus conditions
description: Publication date: 20 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 716 Author(s): Lea Ostorero, Daniele Morgavi, Fabio Arzilli, Georges Boudon, Maurizio Petrelli, Alessandro Pisello, Diego Perugini, Luigi Franciosi, Hélène Balcone-Boissard
abstract: Constraining the magmatic processes that control how magmas differentiate is essential for understanding reservoir dynamics before and during eruptions. Crystallisation and mixing are the two primary processes governing the evolution of magma reservoirs. However, the influence of crystallisation on the physical and chemical mixing of magmas remains poorly constrained, limiting our understanding of textural and chemical evolution of eruptible magma prior to eruptions. Here, we present an experimental study investigating the simultaneous occurrence of crystallisation and dynamic magma mixing using basaltic and dacitic end members at sub-liquidus conditions. Our experiment directly captures the interaction of crystallisation and magma mixing under dynamic conditions, revealing how these processes produce enclave disaggregation, filaments, and compositional gradients in the melt. Our experiment reproduces the interaction of mafic and felsic magmas, and the derived processes of mixing while the crystallisation proceeds. The results indicate that basaltic magmas crystallise rapidly, forming crystal-rich mafic enclaves within a felsic host and producing basaltic andesitic to andesitic melts. Advection promotes stretching and folding, which enhance both chemical exchanges and physical magma mixing effects, leading to enclave disaggregation and the formation of crystal clusters in disequilibrium with the surrounding melt, within a few hours in the investigated experimental setup. We used the parameter σ n 2 (normalized variance) to quantify the mixing efficiency and differential elemental mobilities. This indicates that crystallisation of the mafic magma can promote the evolution of melt compositions that enhances magma mixing efficiency with the more evolved end-member.

title: Synergistic effects of pyrite and thiols on hydroxyl radical production during oxygenation
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Rong Chen, Dan Zheng, Yuting Luo, Menghu Wang, Peng Zhang, Na Yang
abstract: Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) play a crucial role in the biogeochemical processes and the natural attenuation of contaminants in the subsurface. Thiols and pyrite are important reduced sulfur species that are widely distributed in sulfur-reducing environments. However, •OH production in thiol and pyrite coexisting systems has rarely been investigated. Results of this study showed that •OH production was relatively low in thiol-only systems and pyrite-only systems, while substantial •OH production occurred in binary pyrite-thiol systems, with yields enhanced by 13.4–27.5-fold. For instance, at pH 5, •OH accumulations in the 5 mM cysteine system and the 10 g/L pyrite system were 6.4 and 4.0 μM, respectively, while it reached 145.4 μM in the binary pyrite-cysteine systems. The synergistic effects of pyrite and thiols on •OH production decreased with increasing pyrite dosage and solution pH, becoming negligible under alkaline conditions. Density functional theory calculations and electrochemical analyses showed that surface Fe(II) on pyrite can interact with thiols through S and O atoms to form reactive surface complexes. These complexes significantly accelerated the oxidation of both pyrite and thiols, thereby generating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Subsequently, the generated H2O2 reacted with dissolved Fe(II), thiols and thiol radicals to produce •OH. Additionally, dissolved Fe(II) and Fe(III) can directly facilitate •OH production during thiol oxygenation. This synergistic effect between pyrite and thiols enhanced the removal of trichloroethylene from <12% to 24.6% via •OH-driven oxidation. This study revealed a previously overlooked synergistic effect between pyrite and thiols on •OH production, highlighting the often-underappreciated role of reduced sulfur species as sources of •OH in subsurface environments.

title: Stable Ca and Sr isotope responses to ocean acidification during Oceanic Anoxic Event 2
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Lucien Nana Yobo, Chris Holmden, Kimberly V. Lau, Joshua Karas, Alan D. Brandon
abstract: Volcanism-driven ocean acidification has repeatedly disrupted Earth's carbon cycle and ecosystems. Calcium isotopes (δ44/40Ca) provide a potential means of tracking these perturbations, since both the weathering and burial of CaCO3 and the isotopic compositions associated with these fluxes are sensitive to changes in seawater pH. However, the use of δ44/40Ca to reconstruct acidification and infer biocalcification stress is often complicated from overprinting by diagenetic processes. In this paper, we investigate stable Ca (δ44/40Ca) and Sr (δ88/86Sr) isotope responses to ocean acidification during Oceanic Anoxic Event 2 (OAE 2) in a pelagic marine carbonate succession from the Western Interior Seaway. The records are reconstructed using the Iona-1 core in Texas, which fully captures Os isotope evidence for the onset of LIP volcanism that is missing from a previously published Ca isotope record in the Western Interior Seaway in Colorado. Here we show that a negative Ca isotope excursion occupies the missing part of the previously published Western Interior Seaway record, and that it the begins with the onset of large igneous province volcanism as represented by the abrupt shift to lower initial 187Os/188Os isotopic ratios in the core. Box-model simulations show that the negative Ca isotope excursion could be produced through reduced Ca isotope fractionation affecting pelagic carbonate production under conditions of transient acidification stress, followed by rapid recovery through carbonate alkalinity feedback. δ88/86Sr values broadly covary with δ44/40Ca values but deviate from the expected kinetic slope, instead defining a mixing array consistent with seawater-buffered recrystallization. Together, the coupled stable Ca-Sr isotope systematics distinguishes primary acidification-driven signals from diagenetic modification and demonstrate the utility of dual-isotope approaches for tracing volcanism-induced perturbations to the marine carbon cycle.

title: Effects of myo -inositol hexakisphosphate on the Fe(II)-catalyzed transformation of Al-substituted ferrihydrite: A concentration-dependent mechanism and implications for phosphorus geochemical cycling
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Yuan Qiu, Lisong Ma, Biao Wan, Xinran Liang, Shuai Lan, Guanjie Jiang, Yang Li, Qin Zhang, Yupeng Yan
abstract: Poorly crystalline iron hydroxides, such as ferrihydrite (Fh) and its aluminum-substituted counterpart (Al-substituted ferrihydrite, Al-Fh), are ubiquitous in surficial geochemical environments and undergo strong interfacial interactions with organic phosphorus (e.g., myo-inositol hexakisphosphate, phytate, IHP). However, how these interactions regulate the Fe(II)-catalyzed dissolution–recrystallization of Fh and Al-Fh into secondary Fe minerals and consequently influence phosphorus geochemical mobility and sequestration remains unclear. This study systematically investigated the Fe(II)-catalyzed transformation of phytate-preadsorbed Al-Fh via batch experiments and multiple characterizations to elucidate the regulatory role of phytate in governing Fe(II)-catalyzed Al-Fh transformation and phytate repartitioning. Results showed that isomorphous Al substitution inhibited goethite (Gt) nucleation in Fe(II)-catalyzed Al-Fh transformation by decreasing Al-Fh crystallinity and disrupting the periodic Fe–O–Fe crystal lattice arrangement. Fe(II) drove mineral dissolution and secondary phase nucleation via interfacial electron transfer (IET), with catalytic efficiency positively correlated with its concentration. Phytate exerted a concentration-dependent effect: at low concentration (0.5 mM), it impeded the further transformation of lepidocrocite (Lp) to Gt through strong inner-sphere surface complexation of phytate on reactive Fe sites, thereby favoring Lp mineral accumulation. At higher concentrations (≥1.0 mM), it greatly inhibited Al-Fh transformation via a combination of surface complexation, IET inhibition, reactive Fe(II) depletion, and the occupation of mineral dissolution sites, resulting in metastable Lp or amorphous products. Mechanistically, phytate formed stable complexes on Al-Fh surfaces, hindering electron transfer. Concurrently, phytate and Fe(II) generated ternary complexes (≡Fe–IHP–Fe(II)) or surface iron phytate precipitates on minerals, thereby depleting the reactive Fe(II) pool. Throughout transformation, phytate remained strongly sequestered in the solid phase rather than being released into solution due to its strong geochemical interactions with Fe/Al hydroxides. This work elucidates the synergistic regulatory mechanisms of Al and phytate in Al-Fh transformation, offering key theoretical insights into organic phosphorus–iron hydroxide interactions and long-term phosphorus immobilization in Al-rich soils.

title: Quantification of sediment redox capacities under different E h conditions by a modified electrochemical method
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Yingxiao Tian, Peng Zhang, Yuxi Lu, Yanping Cui, Jinguang Xiao, Chenglong Yu, Songhu Yuan
abstract: Sediment redox capacity under different E h conditions is a key parameter for characterizing sediment redox properties and quantifying electron transfer during redox reactions. However, conventional electrochemical methods, while typically suited for standard samples, have limited applicability to heterogeneous sediments. This is primarily due to low reactivity of glassy carbon working electrodes. Here, we developed a modified electrochemical method employing a novel mixed metal oxide (MMO) working electrode. This electrode exhibited significantly higher electrochemical reactivity toward electron mediators and sediments compared to traditional electrodes, enabling more reliable sediment analysis. The accuracy of the MMO-mediated electrochemical system in measuring redox capacities at +0.7, +0.45, +0.25, +0.09, −0.22 and − 0.45 V was verified using various standards, including FeSO4, Fe(OH)3 and iron/manganese minerals, and sediments with different textures, achieving relative standard deviations below 10%. The detection limits for sediment redox capacity in the range of +0.7 to −0.45 V were 3.7–4.9 nmol e−/g (lower limit) and 800–950 μmol e−/g (upper limit). Furthermore, the MMO-mediated electrochemical method reduced the analysis time by half compared to conventional electrochemical methods. Method application showed that the MMO-mediated electrochemical method can effectively characterize sediment redox capacity. For sediment oxygenation, this method can be used to quantify electron transfer processes during the reaction course and reveal the dependence of reactive oxygen species production on electron reactivity under different E h conditions. The MMO-mediated electrochemical method provides a robust and efficient tool for quantifying sediment redox capacity under different E h conditions.

title: Permian crustal growth in the Chinese Altai orogen: Constraints from Sr-Nd-Hf-O-Mg multi-isotope systematics
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Xin Zhang, Yong Tang, Zhan-Long Ma
abstract: Crustal growth is a key process in the formation and evolution of the continental crust. Accurately identifying the contribution of mantle materials to crustal rocks is essential for assessing crustal growth; yet this remains a major challenge. In this study, we present an integrated analysis of zircon UPb geochronology, zircon HfO isotopes, whole-rock major and trace elements, and Sr–Nd–Mg isotope geochemistry for the Chaergan granite, the Dasazi quartz diorite, and their associated dioritic enclaves from the Chinese Altai orogen. The results indicate that the Chaergan granite and Dasazi quartz diorite were emplaced at 277.7 ± 2.5 Ma and 283.4 ± 3.0 Ma, respectively, both during the Permian. The dioritic enclaves within both plutons display coherent elemental differentiation trends (e.g., Cs vs. K/Cs, and Nb/Ta vs. SiO₂, MgO, and TiO₂) and uniform Sr–Nd–Mg isotopic compositions with their host rocks, supporting a cumulate origin. The Chaergan granite is characterized by high (87Sr/86Sr)i ratios (0.706829–0.708711), low εNd(t) (−1.36 to +2.21) and εHf(t) (−3.66 to +4.26) values, high δ18O values (7.84‰ to 10.83‰), and mantle-like Mg isotopic compositions (−0.30‰ to −0.25‰). Combined with elemental ratios (e.g., Nb/U, Ce/Pb, Nb/Ta, Zr/Hf, Nb/Yb, and Th/Yb) from both the granite and its dioritic enclaves, we interpret that its parent magma was derived from subduction-metasomatized subcontinental lithospheric mantle (SCLM) followed by mixing with crustal materials. In contrast, the Dasazi quartz diorite displays low (87Sr/86Sr)i ratios (0.703961 to 0.705862), high εNd(t) (+3.67 to +5.93) and εHf(t) (+5.04 to +8.05) values, high δ18O values (9.17‰ to 10.77‰), and mantle-like Mg isotopic compositions (−0.22‰ to −0.17‰), indicating a magma source solely from subduction-metasomatized SCLM. We propose a post-collisional extensional setting in which upwelling asthenosphere heated the metasomatized mantle, triggering partial melting to produce mafic magmas. These magmas rose and stalled near the Moho, where fractional crystallization formed mafic cumulates. Subsequently, one portion of the magma carried the cumulates upward and crystallized as the Dasazi quartz diorite in the shallow crust, whereas another portion mixed with crustal materials and, also entraining cumulate enclaves, formed the Chaergan granite. Furthermore, our study demonstrates that the Mg isotopic compositions of granites serve as robust tracers of mantle contributions, and that zircon O isotopes can effectively trace subduction-metasomatized SCLM materials in granites. Integrating these findings with a compilation of published Nd–Hf–O isotopic data for Permian granitic rocks in the Chinese Altai orogen, we conclude that continental crustal growth in this region during the Permian was remarkably extensive and active.

title: Calcium isotopic signatures of mid-ocean ridge basalts from the eastern Galápagos Spreading Center that influenced by plume-ridge interaction
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Yujie Shan, Renqiang Liao, Peijun Lin, Jianghong Deng, Long Du, Xin Li, Hongli Zhu, Zhaofeng Zhang, Weidong Sun
abstract: Calcium isotopic heterogeneity has been observed in mantle-derived rocks and such heterogeneity has been attributed to many high-temperature geological processes. However, the effect of plume-ridge interaction on mantle Ca isotopic heterogeneity has yet been well constrained, which may prevent the use of Ca isotopes as a potential tracer for geological processes. Here, to explore the possible effect of plume-ridge interaction on mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORBs), we report high-precision Ca isotopic data together with major-trace element concentrations and SrNd isotopic ratios of a suite of MORB glasses from the eastern Galápagos Spreading Center (EGSC), a key ridge that has interacted with the nearby Galápagos mantle plume. Our results show that the δ44/40Ca of these MORB glasses display a narrow range of 0.72 ± 0.02‰ to 0.81 ± 0.07‰ with an average of 0.78 ± 0.07‰ (2SD, N = 11), which are distinctively lower than the estimate of the Bulk Silicate Earth (BSE, 0.94 ± 0.05‰) and slightly lower than the average of reported nearby Pacific MORBs (0.87 ± 0.08‰, N = 14). Such lightly lower δ44/40Ca of our studied MORB glasses cannot be simply caused by magma evolution or partial melting of spinel peridotites. Instead, the Ca isotopic signature should be inherited from the mantle sources which were influenced by the Galápagos plume, since these MORB glasses have intermediate and positively correlated Ce/Pb and 87Sr/86Sr values between those of the nearby MORBs and basalts from the Galápagos Islands. The Galápagos plume has been proposed to contain ancient recycled oceanic crust and this recycled material can induce the Galápagos plume to have systematically lower δ44/40Ca than the normal MORBs adjacent to the EGSC. Therefore, the slightly lower δ44/40Ca in the Galápagos MORB glasses are most likely caused by plume-ridge interaction. Our study suggests that plume-ridge interaction may serve as a mechanism for transporting recycled materials from plumes into MORB magmas and thereby generating mantle Ca isotopic heterogeneity.

title: Bedrock testing of zircon annealing for detrital provenance studies: Raman and U-Pb analysis in the Adamello batholith (Southern Alps, Italy)
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Alberto Resentini, Marco G. Malusà, Silvia Favaro, Michele Longhi, Massimo Tiepolo, Igor M. Villa, Stefano Zanchetta
abstract: We present a new conceptual model for the interpretation of bedrock and detrital zircon data based on a comparison between theoretical α-damage inferred from U-Pb data and actual α-damage measured by Raman analysis. The model is tested in the Cenozoic Adamello composite batholith in the Southern Alps (Italy), a natural laboratory where the progressive emplacement of successive magmatic bodies has thermally affected both the metamorphic country rocks and the previously emplaced igneous rocks under well-constrained geological conditions. Bedrock samples were collected along a traverse that spans the contact between plutons of different ages and their country rocks. We found that: (i) zircon rims from the Adamello batholith invariably show a complex, but consistent annealing history after crystallization, as induced by subsequent intrusion of younger plutonic bodies; (ii) zircon cores record damage accumulation starting from the age of rim crystallization; (iii) the severity of annealing in country rock zircons correlates with distance from the nearby plutons. Results on bedrock zircon are then exported to a synthetic detrital zircon population to test how the impact of reheating can be detected in detritus. We found that the application of our model allows increasing the resolution of provenance discrimination, providing a level of information approaching the evolution inferred from bedrock data. We conclude that an approach to detrital zircon geochronology complementing detrital U-Pb ages with Raman spectroscopy could open new venues in sediment provenance analysis and could be proficiently used to improve the identification of clastic detritus sources.

title: A daily-weekly-resolved δ 18 O record derived from a modern giant clam shell in the northern South China Sea: Implications for paleoclimate and paleoweather reconstruction
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Chengcheng Liu, Nanyu Zhao, Guozhen Wang, Fan Luo, Shan Liu, Qiuju Yang, Murong Qi, Tao Han, Gang Xue, Miaohong He, Qiuli Li, Guoqiang Tang, Hong Yan
abstract: The aragonite shells of giant clam (Tridacna spp.) with clear daily growth bands have been demonstrated to be an ideal paleoweather archive. However, the current paleoweather proxies of Tridacna spp. are still limited in variety and require further expansion. δ18O, one of the most commonly used geochemical proxies in paleoclimate research, has been widely used for monthly paleoclimate reconstruction in Tridacna spp., which usually reflects sea surface temperature (SST) and seawater δ18O. However, its implication in paleoweather reconstruction is seldomly discussed due to the limitation of data resolution. Here, the daily to weekly resolved Tridacna δ18O profiles from northern South China Sea (SCS) were analyzed using secondary ion mass spectrometer (SIMS). The results show that the daily to weekly resolved δ18O profiles have distinct seasonal cycles, but the derived SST seasonality cannot rule out the possibility of influence from high-frequency fluctuations. More importantly, the daily to weekly resolved δ18O profiles show significant intraseasonal oscillation (ISO). Together with the contemporaneous instrumental data, it is suggested that the ultrahigh resolution Tridacna δ18O has the potential to record the ISO via hydrological and thermal processes.

title: Linear relationships of Gibbs free energy for rare earth element oxide, hydroxide, chloride, fluoride, carbonate, ferrite, and zirconate minerals and crystalline solids
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Ruiguang Pan, Alexander P. Gysi, Artaches A. Migdisov, Nicole C. Hurtig, Chen Zhu
abstract: Rare Earth Elements (REE) are classified as critical minerals and materials essential for the transition from fossil fuels to renewable and clean energy. Accurate thermodynamic properties of REE minerals and other crystalline solids are crucial for geochemical modeling of REE speciation, solubility, and transport in ore deposits and for extraction, chemical processing, and recycling. However, the standard Gibbs free energy of formation (∆G o f,REEX) for these solids vary by 10s kJ mol−1 across different sources from literature. We applied the Sverjensky linear free energy relationship (LFER) to evaluate internal consistency for isostructural REE solid groups and predicted ∆G o f values for solid endmembers for which no experimental measurements are available. By accounting for both ionic radius effects and corresponding aqueous ion properties, the LFER equation, Δ G f , REEX o − β REEX ⋅ r REE Z + = a REEX Δ G n , REE Z + o + b REEX enables accurate ∆G o f value estimates, mostly within 5 kJ mol−1. Here, r REE Z+ represents the Shannon-Prewitt ionic radii (Å) of REEZ+, and ∆G o n,REE Z+ denotes the non-solvation contribution to the ∆G o f of the aqueous REEZ+ ion. X represents the anionic component of the compound REEX. In this study, the parameters a REEX, b REEX, and β REEX were regressed from ∆G o f compilations in the literature for 16 isostructural groups of REE solids. Based on these linear relationships, we recommend a set of internally consistent ∆G o f,REEX values for the REE3+ aqua ions from Shock et al. (1997), and the fitted 142 endmembers of REE oxides, hydroxides, chlorides, fluorides, carbonates, ferrites, and zirconates. These ∆G o f,REEX values were combined with experimental or predicted values of S o, V o, and Cp o from the literature and incorporated into a new dataset, enabling the prediction of thermodynamic properties at high temperature and pressure (e.g., up to 1000 °C and 5 kbar). The log K sp of REE solid dissociation reactions are incorporated into a thermodynamic dataset compatible with the USGS program PHREEQC and the MINES thermodynamic database for use with the GEMS code package. These efforts aid in modeling speciation, solubility, and reactive transport in natural and engineered systems.

title: Granite weathering revealed by magnesium isotopes fractionation: Implications for the flux dynamics and global carbon sink
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Kai Luo, Jin-Long Ma, Fang-Zhen Teng, Gang-Jian Wei, Guan-Hong Zhu, Jia-Rong Liu, Zhuo-Ying Zhang, Zhi-Bing Wang
abstract: Silicate weathering regulates atmospheric CO2 and climate over geological timescales, yet the contribution of granite remains poorly quantified. Here, we present high-resolution Mg isotopic data from a 40 m granite weathering profile in subtropical southern China. Saprolites exhibit significant Mg loss and variation in δ26Mg (−0.24‰ to +0.15‰), with the lowest value in illite and the highest in kaolinite-dominated clays. The pH-dependent adsorption and multistage desorption on clay minerals, particularly kaolinite, control Mg isotope fractionation, with light and heavy isotopes preferentially released under weakly acidic and strongly acidic conditions, respectively. Comparison with Rb, K, Ca, and Li isotopes of the same granite weathering profile reveals a hierarchy of responses to weathering: δ87Rb is a nearly conservative, δ41K reflects K cycling during moderately weathering stages, δ44Ca traces fluid chemistry, and δ26Mg records net secondary mineral formation and delineates zones of chemical alteration. In contrast, δ7Li identifies regions of intense fluid activity and kinetic-controlled weathering fronts. Coupled LiMg isotopes thus enable construct a comprehensive picture of weathering spanning from local, transient fluid-rock interactions to overall, integrated-scale chemical transformations. Our quantitative model yields Mg elemental fluxes of 0.45 to 0.89 mol/cm2/Myr and isotopic fluxes of −0.07‰ to −0.02‰, implying a global CO2 consumption flux of 1.9 × 1012 mol/yr from granite weathering. These results highlight the importance of granite weathering in the global carbon cycle and establishes Mg isotopes as a powerful quantitative tracer of the intensity of silicate weathering and its climate feedbacks.

title: Plastic deformation-induced co-segregation of Au and low-melting-point chalcophile elements along low-angle grain boundaries in pyrite from an epithermal gold deposit
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Jingdan Xiao, Zhuojun Xie, Changzhou Deng, Chenglu Li, Yong Xia, Qinping Tan, Qiqi Zhao, Phillip Gopon
abstract: Plastic deformation-induced microstructures in pyrite, particularly low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs), have been increasingly recognized as potential repositories for Au and low-melting-point chalcophile elements (LMCEs; e.g., Ag, Te, and Bi) in some hydrothermal gold deposits. However, their nanoscale behavior during the plastic deformation of pyrite remains enigmatic in epithermal gold systems. In this study, we systematically investigate the crystallography and geochemistry of pyrite from the Yongxin low-sulfidation epithermal gold deposit, China. Results show that Au- and LMCEs-bearing pyrite exhibits complex misorientation patterns and contains dislocations and LAGBs. Atom probe tomography analyses reveal that Au and LMCEs are preferentially enriched along LAGBs. These elements exhibit significant depletion in the regions adjacent to the LAGBs. In the Y-Z projection plane, the LAGBs display a planar feature, consisting of a series of semi-parallel compositional bands of Au and LMCEs. Additionally, quartz closely associated with pyrite shows grain orientation spread values typically below 2° and an average grain size of 8 μm. These findings collectively suggest that pyrite in the Yongxin deposit underwent significant plastic deformation via dislocation creep, during which Au and LMCEs gradually segregated into LAGBs through a dislocation-impurity pair diffusion mechanism. This study underscores the critical role of plastic deformation in element remobilization and re-enrichment. Furthermore, elemental segregation observed within microstructures implies that interpretations of micron-scale geochemical anomalies as mineral inclusions should be treated with caution.

title: Interaction of transition metals with carbonate green rust: Environmental applications and insights into ancient oceans
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Ichiko Sugiyama, Itay Halevy
abstract: Carbonate green rust (GRCO 3 ) is a mixed-valence double hydroxide mineral found in suboxic and anoxic natural and engineered environments. It is highly reactive towards dissolved metals, as shown in past studies of GRCO 3 -metal interactions. However, such interactions under conditions representative of modern and ancient marine systems remains poorly constrained, as does the fate of metals during GRCO 3 aging and transformation into stable Fe-bearing minerals. Constraining these processes is critical for predicting long-term metal mobility and retention in marine and groundwater systems and for understanding the biogeochemical cycles and reduction–oxidation dynamics of metals in the anoxic and ferruginous Precambrian ocean, and the supply of bioessential metals to ancient microbial communities. To address this knowledge gap, we investigated GRCO 3 co-precipitation with Cd II , Co II , Cu II , Mn II , Ni II , and Zn II (0.1–300 μ M) in seawater-analog solutions at pH 8.0 under anoxic conditions. In aging experiments at 1 μ M metal concentrations over 13 months, we assessed metal retention during GRCO 3 transformation. After 3 days, metal uptake generally followed the Irving–Williams series (Cd < Mn < Ni < Co < Cu ≥ Zn), except Ni and Co, which were reversed due to Co oxidation. Over 13 months, all metals except Mn were taken up completely, while Mn uptake increased gradually but was not quantitative. Cu and Zn exhibited effectively irreversible uptake, likely through co-precipitation at Fe II sites and, for Cu, also reduction to Cu 0 and precipitation. Mn and Co were slowly oxidized to Mn III/IV and Co III , respectively, while Ni II and Cd II uptake increased gradually, reflecting slow kinetics of adsorption or structural incorporation. These findings provide mechanistic insight into divalent metal uptake by GRCO 3 and demonstrate how solution composition, aqueous speciation, mineral transformations, and aging govern metal retention in both modern and ancient suboxic and anoxic environments. In light of these findings, we highlight the complexity of interpreting proxy records preserved in Precambrian Fe-enriched sedimentary archives.

title: Assessing the applicability of methods for calculating 234 U recoil loss factor in the comminution age model
description: Publication date: 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 715 Author(s): Shijun Wang, Chao Li, Songyang Ma, Yulong Guo, Weibo Lai, Junfei Chen, Wei Yue, Maoyong He, Shiming Wan, Shouye Yang
abstract: The comminution age method estimates the time elapsed since the physical weathering of bedrock into detrital sediment, offering a promising tool for quantifying the timescale of earth surface processes, e.g. catchment weathering and erosion. This method is now extensively used in sediment source-to-sink investigations across various environments, including fluvial, marine, aeolian, and glacial sediment systems. The fundamental principle of this method relies on quantifying the time-dependent 234U depletion caused by α-recoil effects in sediment grains. Nevertheless, significant uncertainty persists regarding the model's key parameter, the 234U recoil loss factor (f α ). This study utilized a suite of well-characterized typical East Asian sediment samples with precisely constrained f α values, including ancient deposits from the Changjiang (Yangtze) River Delta, Chinese loess, and the South China Sea (SCS), to evaluate the applicability of various methods for estimating f α . Our results show that f α is significantly affected by the specific surface area of sediment particles. Compared to other models hindered by the limitations of specific surface area measurements or overly simplified grain morphologies, the weighted geometric model (Model 2) is expected to be a more robust approach for calculating f α . However, this model is heavily restricted by the empirical values assigned to maximum surface roughness (λ max ) and maximum aspect ratio (β max ). In this study, Monte Carlo simulations were employed to objectively constrain the values of λ max and β max . The results revealed that valid solutions for λ max can reach up to 317 and β max up to 7.1, which differ significantly from the empirical constants used in previous studies. Applying the simulated outputs to modern Changjiang sediments yielded a comminution age of 720 kyr (95% CI: 580–963 kyr), substantially older than previous estimates of 400–600 kyr. Furthermore, based on the simulation results, the comminution ages calculated for Changjiang sediments deposited during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) ranged from 354 to 593 kyr, which also deviates significantly from the 141–310 kyr estimated by previous studies. This study not only provides a more reliable timescale for the source-to-sink processes of East Asian sediments but also offers a new methodological reference for the application of the weighted geometric model and the comminution age method.

title: N analysis in nominally N-free silicate minerals and glasses using NanoSIMS
description: Publication date: Available online 19 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Aindrila Pal, Rajdeep Dasgupta, Detlef Rogalla, Evelyn Füri, Julien Boulliung
abstract: Quantifying trace nitrogen (N) in nominally N-free silicate minerals and glasses is essential for constraining deep N cycling and N partitioning during magmatic and planetary differentiation, yet remains analytically challenging at the parts per million by weight (ppm) level. We develop and benchmark a NanoSIMS protocol for in situ N analysis in common silicates using NO− secondary ions, supported by a suite of matrix-matched reference materials spanning ~1 ppm to 1.6 wt% N. Reference materials include (i) well-characterized 1-atm gas-mixing experimental 14N bearing silicate glasses, (ii) high-pressure experimental 14N bearing silicate glass, and (iii) 15N-implanted olivine, clinopyroxene, garnet, and silicate glasses. N in implanted standards is independently quantified by Nuclear Resonance Reaction Analysis (NRRA) to constrain implantation profiles and peak concentrations. Using 29Si− as an internal normalizer and high mass-resolving power to mitigate molecular interferences, we derive session- and matrix-specific calibrations, quantify analytical background, and determine limits of detection of ~0.1–0.3 ppm N for silicate minerals and glasses (session-dependent). Mineral calibrations are linear over 0–1000 ppm and exhibit matrix-dependent sensitivity, requiring matrix- and session-specific slopes. For glasses, 14N16O−/29Si− provides the most robust quantification, whereas 15N16O− can be biased by unresolved 29SiH2 − contributions and implantation-related effects in hydrous/amorphous matrices. Application to previously published N-doped clinopyroxene–melt experiments yields NanoSIMS N concentrations consistent with independent EPMA measurements, validating the calibration strategy. The protocol and reference framework enable reproducible micron-scale N determinations in silicate materials relevant to experimental petrology and natural samples.

title: Xenon isotope composition of the La Palma mantle plume (Canary Islands): assessing upper mantle versus plume mantle source evolution
description: Publication date: Available online 19 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): David V. Bekaert, B. Marty, Alan M. Seltzer, Yinlei Hao, David J. Byrne, Z. Conseil, Eleazar Padrón
abstract: Determining the xenon (Xe) isotope composition of Earth's deep-mantle reservoirs is key to constraining early terrestrial volatile acquisition and subsequent evolution. Here, we employ dynamic mass spectrometry to characterize the Xe isotope composition of the Dos Aguas CO2-rich, cold mineral spring (La Palma, Canary Islands), previously shown to exhibit the highest 3He/4He reported from the Canarian archipelago (10.85 Ra). Although the plume mantle-derived Xe contribution is small (≤0.8%), its signature matches that of the convecting upper mantle (e.g., δ129Xe*/δ136Xe* ≈ 1; i.e., with comparable 129Xe* and 136Xe* excesses relative to air). This result aligns with the growing evidence that plume mantle- and upper mantle-derived sources are colinear in δ129Xe vs. δ136Xe and δ129Xe*/δ136Xe* vs. δ130Xe*/136Xe* spaces. For a decade, however, the latter space was considered a powerful means to discriminate between both mantle sources. Here, we use numerical modelling of mantle Xe evolution to answer a simple question: could the distinct evolutions of the highly degassed, convecting upper mantle (primary source of fissiogenic 136Xe*: extant 238U) and the primitive, minimally degassed plume mantle (primary source of 136Xe*: extinct 244Pu) have coincidentally converged towards a unique δ129Xe*/δ136Xe* ≈ 1. Our model shows that, despite a two orders of magnitude difference in the total extents of degassing, such a coincidence cannot be discarded. An alternative scenario would be that deep, primitive plume mantle sources akin to La Palma may also be dominated by extant 238U fission rather than extinct 244Pu, potentially requiring deep mantle sources to be far more degassed than previously considered.

title: Tracing the sources of noble gases for helium prospectivity in the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin
description: Publication date: Available online 19 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Stuart M.V. Gilfillan, Emma Martin-Roberts, Nicholas Utting, Rachel Utley, Kirk Osadetz, Don Lawton
abstract: Constraining the origin and understanding how fluids move through the Earth's crust is critical in assessing the accumulation of globally important gas reserves such as helium and hydrogen. Noble gases serve as useful tracers in natural gases due to their inertness and are routinely used to identify the origin and migration of subsurface fluids in order to resolve the physical migratory processes that occur in the subsurface. Here we report a new compilation of 53 noble gas isotope and concentration measurements from the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin (WCSB) obtained from 46 natural gas wells that sample the regional stratigraphy from the Upper Cretaceous to the Cambrian. Previous results show evidence of radiogenic noble gases present in the Alberta basin formations. Helium isotope ratios indicate resolvable mantle derived helium (3He), likely from Eocene age intrusions within the basin. Increases in the predominantly radiogenic derived 4He, 21Ne* and 40Ar* are identified in the deepest samples, while ratios of 21Ne/22Ne, 40Ar*/36Ar and 21Ne*/36Ar also increase with proximity to the Precambrian basement. We infer this indicates a radiogenic flux is present, which most probably originates from the Precambrian basement. Variation exists throughout the basin, specifically in the youngest formations which exhibit enrichments in the lightest noble gases (4He and 21Ne) when compared with the heaviest (40Ar). We propose that this is due to a combination of solubility-controlled fractionation and the preferential release of lighter noble gases from minerals in a lower temperature regime. The calculation of initial 4He in groundwaters in a closed system model demonstrates that the deepest WCSB formations (Cambrian to Upper Devonian) have some of the oldest 4He ages compared to their formation ages, suggesting an external supply of radiogenic He is required, likely from a basement source. Higher in the stratigraphy, 4He ages both older and younger than the respective lithologies are observed, providing evidence of frequent groundwater recharge or glacial flushing events. This also suggests that some of the shallowest formations require an external source of He, implying an open-system cross-formational flow of radiogenic noble gas within WCSB. We identify the most prospective formation for possible He accumulation in WCSB to be the porous Devonian or deeper Cambrian formations, due to their proximity to basement lithologies.

title: Kaolinite genesis and the formation of REE ion adsorption deposits
description: Publication date: Available online 18 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Martin Smith, Eva Marquis, Liam Hardy, Adrian Boyce, Kathryn Goodenough, Guillaume Estrade, Jindrich Kynicky, Cheng Xu
abstract: Ion adsorption deposits (IAD), where the Rare Earth Elements (REE) occur adsorbed onto clay minerals in weathered granitoids, are a major source of the critical REE. In this study we aim to test if there is an influence from the climatic or epigenetic conditions of kaolinite formation on the potential for IAD formation. Samples were collected from logged transects from 3 sites with clay adsorbed REE (Zhaibei, China; Ambohimirahavavy, Madagascar; Monchique, Portugal) and analysed for bulk REE content and ammonium sulphate leachable REE, followed by kaolinite separation, characterisation and stable isotope analysis to determine the conditions of formation. Saprolite weathering zones are enriched in the REE relative to bedrock, with leachable fractions between 10 and 90%. Kaolinite dD and δ18O indicate formation from 86 to ~20 °C. Higher mean T for Portugal and Madagascar reflects the presence of late epigenetic hydrothermal kaolinite prior to weathering. Once the effects of position in the weathering profile have been isolated using the sign and magnitude of the Ce anomaly, the % leachable REE correlates with T, with high % leachable at lower formation T. Analysis of oriented clay mounts by XRD shows that kaolinite crystallinity is variable between sites and within profiles. The variation in leachable fraction REE correlates to increased adsorption onto finer kaolinite crystallite sizes, with corresponding enhanced surface area, which in turn can be related to kaolinite formation conditions. Kaolinite crystallinity is major factor in formation of economic IAD mineralisation, alongside intensity of weathering and changing pH in soil profiles. Hydrothermal kaolinite is unfavourable for the formation of ion adsorption deposits compared to weathering kaolinite.

title: Phonolite – Carbonate interaction in the Somma-Vesuvius plumbing system: experimental insights into the mechanisms of limestone assimilation, crustal limestone melting and Campanian magma differentiation
description: Publication date: Available online 18 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Knuever Marco, Perinelli Cristina, Gaeta Mario, Pavese Raffaela, Mele Daniela, Sulpizio Roberto, Pisello Alessandro, Dellino Pierfrancesco
abstract: The interaction of magmas with host-rocks is a common process in magmatic systems. Interaction with carbonate-bearing lithologies is of major interest since the thermometamorphic reactions during magma‑carbonate interaction, may release CO₂ affecting eruptive behaviour. The Somma-Vesuvius volcanic system is built on a km-thick Mesozoic carbonate platform, with evidence of intense interaction in the form of carbonate-xenoliths in juvenile pumices and as skarns. Nevertheless, the timescales and mechanisms of magma‑carbonate interactions remain poorly constrained. Here we present an experimental study on the interaction of a dry Vesuvius' phonolite melt with a high-Ca limestone and a dolomitic limestone. We conducted the experiments in a piston cylinder apparatus at 600 MPa, temperatures of 950 °C and 1200 °C and interaction times of 0–60 min. Bubble nucleation (CO₂ release) has been observed in all experiments. The dolomitic limestone is assimilated via an AFC-process, creating a skarn-like assemblage of periclase-bearing dolomite, forsterite, clinopyroxene and a Ca + Mg-enriched melt. The high-Ca limestone exhibits a partial melting texture, that includes the formation of a Na-K-Ca chloride carbonate melt due to direct diffusive transport of alkalis and chlorine from the dry phonolite melt into the limestone. The melting of limestones at crustal conditions may affect magma differentiation trends in Campanian magmas, especially the Na₂O/K₂O ratio. The reported assimilation timescales of 30–60 min at 1200 °C for both limestones are however maximum estimates, as a dry phonolitic melt was used at pressures exceeding those to be expected in the Vesuvius plumbing system (<200 MPa). The presence of water would greatly accelerate limestone assimilation.

title: Impact of volcanic volatile releases on Mesozoic terrestrial biotas in northern China
description: Publication date: Available online 14 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Lu Wang, Jia Liu, Etienne Deloule, Xiao-Yan Gu, Qi-Hu Xu, Qun-Ke Xia
abstract: Volcanic eruptions significantly modify surface environments and climate, with profound effects on biota across various spatial and temporal scales. The spatiotemporal evolution of the Mesozoic Yanliao and Jehol biotas in northern China—two world-renowned terrestrial lagerstätten—correlates with Jurassic to early Cretaceous volcanic activity during the destruction of the North China craton on a million-year timescale. However, the specific impacts of contemporaneous volcanic activity on terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. In this study, we measured chlorine and/or sulfur concentrations in phenocrysts of clinopyroxene and amphibole, as well as apatite inclusions from Jurassic volcanic rocks in northern China. Using experimentally calibrated mineral-melt partition/exchange coefficients, we quantitatively estimate the original volatile concentrations of Cl = 1214–3432 ppm and S = 669–1514 ppm for the Haifanggou volcanic rocks associated with the development phase of the Yanliao Biota, and Cl = 5428–9475 ppm and S = 1158–2011 ppm for the Upper Tiaojishan/Lanqi volcanic rocks associated with the decay phase of the Yanliao Biota. Our results, integrated with previous studies, suggest that substantial emissions of toxic gases (Cl and S)—which triggered episodic acid rain, soil erosion, vegetation damage, water contamination, and wildfires—likely contributed, at least in part, to the decline of the Yanliao Biota and hindered the emergence of the Jehol Biota. In contrast, relatively limited volatile fluxes, reduced delivery of harmful elements, and the sufficient supply of nutrient elements from volcanic products may have fostered favorable conditions that supported the development and flourishing of both the Yanliao and Jehol biotas.

title: Arsenopyrite-driven oxidative dissolution of stibnite: pH-dependent ROS effect and antimony transformation
description: Publication date: Available online 14 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Kequn Li, Jingkang Zhang, Hao Liu, Liyuan Ma, Jianwei Zhou, Xingjie Wang
abstract: The fate of antimony (Sb) in mining environment is markedly influenced by the coexisting arsenic and iron sulfide minerals. However, the mechanism underlying the effect of arsenopyrite (FeAsS) on the oxidative dissolution of stibnite (Sb2S3) under ambient pH conditions remains unclear. This study investigated the release of antimony from stibnite associated with arsenopyrite under acidic and neutral conditions. Arsenopyrite promoted stibnite dissolution at both pH values, with total Sb released at pH 3.0 (10.03 mg·L−1) being 3.65 times that at pH 7.0 (2.75 mg·L−1), and Sb(V) predominated in solution. Under neutral conditions, Fe (oxyhydr)oxides accumulated on the surfaces of arsenopyrite, diminishing its promoting effect on stibnite dissolution. The Sb(III)-arsenopyrite interaction experiments demonstrated that the arsenopyrite significantly facilitated the Sb(III) oxidation with 95.04% conversion at pH 3.0. In contrast, only 4.85% Sb(V) formed at pH 7.0, far lower than that in the neutral stibnite-arsenopyrite system (96.98%). The suppressed oxidation is likely attribute to the higher Sb(III) loading, which enhanced the adsorption and passivation effects of arsenopyrite. Quenching experiments further confirmed that the ROS generated through Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox cycling on arsenopyrite surfaces serve as the predominant oxidants responsible for stibnite dissolution and Sb(III) oxidation. Notably, hydroxyl radicals (•OH) were identified as the predominant ROS under acidic conditions, while the ROS generation was inhibited under neutral conditions, where non-radical pathways or surface-contact oxidation may prevail. Overall, this study reveals a pH-dependent oxidative dissolution mechanism in the stibnite-arsenopyrite co-existing system, advancing understanding of Sb geochemical behavior in sulfide-rich environments.

title: Mineral/melt partitioning of the first-row transition elements, Ga, and Ge during lower-crustal crystallization: Controls on deep metal fractionation in hydrous arcs
description: Publication date: Available online 3 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Linghan H. Liu, Hongluo L. Zhang, Zhaochong Zhang, Xuan Guo, Jintuan Wang, Ekaterina S. Kiseeva, Meng Wang, Fang Huang
abstract: The geochemical behavior of first-row transition elements (FRTEs), Ga, and Ge during arc magma evolution is fundamentally framed by fractional crystallization, yet quantitative constraints on their mineral–melt partitioning under hydrous, lower-crustal conditions remain limited. New experimental partition coefficients(D) determined at 1.25 GPa and 850–1100 °C reveal similar compatibility sequences in amphibole and clinopyroxene, ranging from high (D Ni up to ~102) to weak (e.g., Mn, Zn, Ga, Ge; D as low as ~0.9). Conversely, plagioclase is largely incompatible for most elements except Ga, which is weakly compatible. Using these data and compiled literature values, we developed a multivariate parameterization of D as a function of temperature, mineral composition, and melt composition. The results indicate that water content in the melt may have a stronger influence on Ds for nominally anhydrous minerals (NAMs) than on amphibole. Model application shows that an element's sensitivity to fractionation path (continuous vs. episodic) is largely predictable from its bulk partition coefficient (D bulk). Elements are classified into three types: (1) path-sensitive (i.e., Cr, Ni), with high D bulk, strongly depleted in melt and enriched in deep cumulates; (2) path-insensitive (e.g., Cu, Zn), whose concentrations evolve with total crystallinity regardless of path; and (3) moderately path-sensitive (e.g., Sc, Co), with D bulk relying on mineral assemblage and resulting in path-modulated depletion. This framework deciphers crust-scale metal sorting in arcs, exemplified by the antithetical fates of Cr, Ni (compatible) and Cu (incompatible, as modeled), and provides a quantitative basis for the petrogenetic complementarity between deep cumulate-hosted and shallow magmatic-hydrothermal mineralization.

title: 3D phase-field modeling of limestone dissolution process induced by CO 2
description: Publication date: Available online 21 March 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Wenchao Dou, Mian Lin
abstract: The evolution of the fluid-solid interface caused by dissolution in carbonate rocks leads to changes in reservoir seepage performance and mechanical properties; therefore, it is necessary to elucidate this process. At present, the chemical reaction rates measured in experiments are directly used in most numerical models describing the fluid-solid interface evolution, which greatly limits their application and expansion. In this study, the phase-field method was used to simulate limestone dissolution. The chemical kinetics model is introduced into the phase-field model so that it can simulate the three-dimensional evolution process of limestone dissolution under different temperature, pressure and fluid chemistry conditions. Our simulation results show that the phase-field model can reproduce the evolution process of the fluid-solid interface of limestone dissolution. In addition, phase-field simulation can accurately calculate the reactive surface area (RSA), which is superior to other RSA prediction models commonly used in continuous medium models. Through the pore structure image obtained by phase-field simulation, the specific surface area and tortuosity can be easily calculated; thus, the KC equation was used to predict the permeability, and the accuracy is significantly higher than that of other simple porosity-permeability relationships. In addition, our model can also be used to evaluate the influence of different physical and chemical conditions on limestone dissolution.

title: The Sedimentary geochemistry and paleoenvironments project phase 2 data release: An open data resource for the study of Earth's environmental history
description: Publication date: Available online 19 February 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Úna C. Farrell, Hunter C. Olson, Maya O. Thompson, Michelle L. Abshire, Oyeleye O. Adeboye, Anne-Sofie C. Ahm, Lewis J. Alcott, Thomas J. Algeo, Ross P. Anderson, Arif H. Ansari, Lucas Pinto Heckert Bastos, Kohen W. Bauer, Brian Beaty, Justin E. Birdwell, Fred T. Bowyer, Jochen J. Brocks, Tessa Brunoir, James F. Busch, Donald E. Canfield, Fabrício A. Caxito
abstract: Geochemical data from sedimentary rocks are the primary source of information regarding Earth's surface evolution through time, including its air and water envelopes and interactions with life and deep Earth processes. The Sedimentary Geochemistry and Paleoenvironments Project (SGP) is a scientific consortium centered around open data and community-driven development of cyberinfrastructure tools and resources for sedimentary geochemistry and Earth history. Here we describe the SGP Phase 2 data release, which focused on incorporating Paleoproterozoic and Mesoproterozoic (2500–1000 million years ago) data and better accommodating carbonate data. This data release was built through the involvement of >200 researchers worldwide in academia, government, and industry, and provides the largest available public data resource for our user community in the academic fields of geochemistry, sedimentology, tectonics, paleontology, Earth history, and paleoclimate, as well as the petroleum and minerals industries. The dataset now encompasses 126,006 samples and 4,132,371 geochemical analyses. In addition to direct entry by SGP Team Members, we have ingested and incorporated datasets from the Geoscience Australia OZCHEM database, the Alberta Geological Survey, and the Deep-Time Marine Sedimentary Element Database (DM-SED) compilation. This paper details sampling in the Phase 2 dataset with respect to age, geography, lithology, and other geological characteristics, documents access via our search website and API, discusses possible issues and/or biases in the dataset that could impact analyses, describes plans for governance and stewardship of data from Indigenous lands, and serves as the citable reference paper for the data release.

title: A prompt-guided differentiable physics model for flood forecasting in data-scarce basins
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Jiru Zhang, Jun Feng, Runliang Xia, Pingping Shao, Xin Chi
abstract: Flood forecasting remains one of the long-standing challenges in hydrology. Most existing approaches, trained on single or limited data-rich basins, struggle to transfer hydrological knowledge to data-scarce ones. Moreover, these models neglect the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of hydrological processes, and lack explicit physical constraints on flood dynamics during training, which limit their physical consistency and predictive accuracy. Therefore, we propose a prompt-guided differentiable physics model (PGDP) for accurate and interpretable flood forecasting in data-scarce basins. Specifically, we introduce a static-temporal (ST) masking strategy for pretraining to capture complex spatiotemporal dynamics. Additionally, we design a dual-path prompting approach to enable robust knowledge transfer and improve generalization in data-scarce catchments. The first path leverages learnable prompts to adaptively retrieve relevant temporal patterns, while the second path introduces supplementary prior knowledge about physical parameter distributions through discrete prompt embeddings. Importantly, the interpretability of the PGDP is established by adding a differentiable physics simulation layer, which integrates the governing equations of the Xin’anjiang model into a differentiable computational graph through end-to-end training. Furthermore, under the guidance of evapotranspiration, runoff smoothness, and water balance principles, we design three loss functions of the proposed model to ensure the predicted results are more consistent with the laws of flood physics. Experiments on the CAMELS dataset demonstrate that PGDP outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy, especially in data-scarce basins. Compared with benchmark models, it achieves substantial average improvements of 28.43% in NSE and 20.26% in KGE across eight data-scarce basins.

title: Projected response of global rainfall-induced landslides to future climate change
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Kailiang Zhao, Haijun Qiu, Ya Liu, Guoqing Yang, Zijing Liu, Wanqi Luo, Yaru Zhu, Guoyu Wang, Mohib Ullah
