This study aims to both apply the Weibull distribution to more than 47,000 DSDs detected at Palermo (Italy) and El Teularet (Spain) experimental sites and deduce theoretically relationships for estimating the rainfall kinetic power and momentum of a DSD distributed as Weibull law having known parameters. The study confirms that the theoretical Weibull distribution can accurately reproduce measured DSDs, with highly consistent fitting results using the moment method (MM) for estimating its parameters. The results indicate that rainfall kinetic power and momentum are closely related to the characteristics of the DSD. No statistically significant correlation between the parameters of the Weibull distribution and rainfall intensity is detected. Moreover, the analysis highlights that the η parameter turns out to be related to the coefficient of variation of the DSD, and the parameter N0 represents the total number of drops, making the Weibull distribution physically based. Furthermore, a comparison between the Weibull and Ulbrich distributionsallowsfor the conclusion that, although both models exhibit similar performance in terms of fitting and reliability when describing rainfall kinetic power and momentum, the Weibull distribution offers advantages related to parameter estimation. Specifically, its parameters, unlike those of Ulbrich,possessaphysical, and not merely statistical, significance. The study concludes that the Weibull distribution is highly reliable for characterizing rainfall kinetic power and momentum in two experimental sites located in the Mediterranean region, and rainfall intensity cannot serve as a variable to comprehensively represent the characteristics of precipitation.

title: Threshold responses of diatom community to hydrological changes in an alpine peatland based on long-term (2014–2020) monitoring data
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Xu Chen, Junlu Li, Jia Peng, Shuangyu Xu, Jun He, Shumin Qiao, Linghan Zeng, Xianyu Huang
abstract: There is an increasing need to detect ecological thresholds for the establishment of numerical environmental criteria for ecosystem restoration. Peatlands have important implications for global carbon cycling and biodiversity conservation, while information on threshold responses of biotic communities to ecohydrological changes in peatlands is limited. Based on long-term (2014–2020) monitoring data, this study explored how diatom species and functional traits (i.e., life forms, cell sizes and ecological guilds) responded to ecohydrological changes in Dajiuhu Peatland, a Ramsar site in central China. Ordination analyses revealed that diatom species composition was significantly related to depth to the water table (DWT) and pH, while functional trait composition was significantly associated with DWT and electrical conductivity. Taxa indicator threshold analyses (TITAN) indicated that diatom species community changed substantially at DWT greater than 12 cm or at pH greater than 4.58, while functional trait community changed substantially at DWT greater than 12.5 cm or at conductivity greater than 17.80 μS cm−1. The ecological thresholds detected by diatom species and functional traits can serve as numerical environmental criteria for the restoration of this Ramsar site, as well as similar subtropical peatlands. The results highlight the benefit of using both diatom species and functional traits to improve our understanding of underlying ecological processes in peatland ecosystems.

title: Unraveling dissolved inorganic nitrogen dynamics in a sandy beach: The role of tidal forces and aquifer heterogeneity
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Cheng Xing, Yan Zhang, Hongkai Qi, Ding He, Yi Liu
abstract: Coastal groundwater is one of the major nitrogen (N) sources for marine ecosystems, yet the estimates of the N flux have a large uncertainty due to limited understanding of in-situ biogeochemical processes in the intertidal aquifer under the influence of tidal fluctuations and aquifer heterogeneity. In this study, a high-resolution intertidal groundwater monitoring across spring-neap tidal cycles revealed vertically stratified dissolved inorganic N (DIN) speciation controlled by redox zonation. Nitrate (NO3 – > 230 μM) dominated the shallow zone ( 340 μM) in the deep zone (> 1.5 m), where sediments consist of high-organic content and low-permeability marine deposits. A two-endmember mixing model indicates the local production of NO3 – and NH4 + in the aquifer. The co-occurrence of high NH4 + and high salinity in the low-permeability, anoxic, organic-rich marine deposits suggests DIN production through the remineralization of soil organic matter (SOM) possibly driven by reduction of iron (Ⅲ) oxide and sulfate. NO3 – enrichment in the shallow oxic zone (< 1.5 m) is a result of strong nitrification. Sediment incubation with labeled δ15N-NH4 + showed nitrification rate was 10-fold higher in the shallow zone than the deep zone. From neap to spring tides, submarine groundwater discharge increased by 15% from 6.94 to 8.00 m2 d-1, while DIN export decreased by 7% from 1.24 × 103 to 1.15 × 103 mmol m−1 d-1. This paradox is led by the enhanced flow dynamics during spring tide, which shortens average groundwater residence time from 7.15 to 6.20 d, thereby limits remineralization of SOM. Our findings highlight intertidal aquifers as dynamic biogeochemical reactors strongly influenced by aquifer heterogeneity and tidal forces. Locally geogenic N is one of the major sources of coastal groundwater N in addition to inputs from terrestrial groundwater.

title: Systematic evaluation of atmospheric forcing, surface datasets, and mesh effects on kilometer-scale land surface and river modeling
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Lingcheng Li, Gautam Bisht, Donghui Xu, Dalei Hao, Chang Liao, Dongyu Feng, Zeli Tan, Hongyi Li, Mingjie Shi, Tian Zhou, L. Ruby Leung
abstract: Earth system models are advancing toward kilometer-scale resolution to capture local climate impacts and extremes. High-resolution land and river modeling depends on multiple factors, including mesh, surface datasets, and atmospheric forcing, but their relative effects at kilometer scales remain unquantified. We evaluated five Energy Exascale Earth System Model land and river configurations over the Mid-Atlantic region using two meshes (1/8° structured versus variable-resolution unstructured mesh), two surface datasets (default versus newly developed), and three atmospheric forcings (NLDAS, MSWX, GSWP). Evaluation against satellite, reanalysis, and in situ benchmarks across water, energy, and carbon cycles quantifies how these factors affect model performance. Forcing selection produces the largest effects on simulations (12–99% of baseline bias change across variables), followed by surface datasets (5–75%) and mesh (up to 21%). Forcing effects vary by variable, with MSWX reducing biases for snow water equivalent, evapotranspiration, albedo, temperature, and gross primary productivity, GSWP for snow cover and runoff, and NLDAS for soil moisture and streamflow. The use of newly developed surface datasets improves gross primary productivity and evapotranspiration but increases soil moisture and albedo biases due to current modeling limitations. Variable-resolution unstructured mesh improves the simulation of small-basin streamflow through better capturing drainage networks, though mesh minimally affects other land variables. These findings provide important guidance for high-resolution modeling development and actionable science.

title: Attributing terrestrial water storage changes on the Tibetan Plateau to climate and human drivers using a hybrid deep learning approach
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Zhiqiang Yang, Aili Yang, Xiong Zhou
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau (TP), referred to as “Water Tower” for Asia, is highly sensitive to both climate change and anthropogenic activities. However, assessing the spatiotemporal dynamics of terrestrial water storage (TWS) and attributing its changes across the TP remains challenging. This is primarily due to discontinuous satellite observations and the complex interactions between climatic drivers and potentially human-related influences. To address these limitations, we develop a VMD‑CNN‑LSTM‑based TWS Prediction and Hierarchical Attribution (VCLHA) framework. VCLHA can quantify the independent contributions of climatic factors (precipitation, evapotranspiration, runoff, and temperature) and a residual component potentially associated with human activities to TWSC. The evaluation results demonstrate that the framework has robust performance, achieving a Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) value of 0.983. Robustness is further supported by intercomparison with independent GRACE-like reconstructions (e.g., GRACE-REC, CSRM-Bayesian, and BNML_TWSA) during the GRACE/GRACE-FO observational gap (July 2017–May 2018), showing consistent plateau-mean evolution. The prediction results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with water increases of 1.87 mm yr−1 in northern TP and severe water decreases of 8.17mm yr−1 in the south. The precipitation is identified as the dominant climatic driver, explaining 43.2% of the variance in TWS change. However, while the residual component potentially associated with human activities shows no clear long-term trend (0.05 mm yr−1), it exhibits strong seasonality, characterized by positive effects in spring and negative effects in summer (−2.81 mm) and autumn (−1.62 mm). This seasonal variability amplifies water-storage deficits during summer–autumn (July–October), particularly in southern and outflow basins. These findings provide quantitative evidence for the relative roles of climate variability and human-related influence in regional water storage variability, thereby supporting adaptive and region-specific water-resource management strategies on the TP. Plain Language Summary. The Tibetan Plateau (TP) supplies freshwater to many of Asia’s major rivers and supports hundreds of millions of people downstream. However, it is challenging to determine how much recent changes in water availability are related to climate change and human-related influences. In this study, we develop a hybrid deep learning framework to reconstruct satellite gravity observations and to assess the relative roles of natural processes and a residual component potentially associated with human activities in water storage change. From 2003 to 2023, climate-related processes have led to a steady long-term decline in water storage (−0.10 mm per year). While the residual component potentially associated with human activities did not exhibit a consistent long-term trend, it had a pronounced seasonal impact, contributing to water gains in spring but intensifying losses in summer (−2.81 mm) and autumn (−1.62 mm). These seasonal deficits were most severe in southern, downstream basins, whereas northern and interior regions showed partial recovery in spring. Precipitation was found to be the most important climate factor influencing water storage. These insights can help improve drought preparedness, irrigation planning, and reservoir management as climate change continues to reshape the regional water cycle.

title: Storage–supply regulation and rainfall responses driven by thermokarst lakes in permafrost-degrading catchments
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Junhao Cui, Jia Qin, YongJian Ding, Yongyong Zhang, Bingfeng Yang, Feiteng Wang, Xiaobo He, Guangxi Ding
abstract: Thermokarst lakes are key indicators of permafrost degradation on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP), yet their catchment-scale hydrological role under rainfall remains poorly understood. To address this, we conducted a paired-catchment study in the source region of the Yellow River, comparing a thermokarst-lake catchment (TLC) containing hundreds of lakes with a nearby non-lake catchment (nTLC). We combined annual water-balance closure with event-scale diagnostics, including soil–water storage change, groundwater-level change, lake-stage change, and hysteresis-based metrics to characterize storage–release behavior. Our results show contrasting annual water-retention outcomes: the TLC exhibited net storage depletion (−38.48 mm), whereas the nTLC showed net storage gain (+63.60 mm), and this contrast remained under both full and simplified closure formulations. At the event-scale, the TLC showed stronger rainfall-normalized subsurface responses than the nTLC, with groundwater responsiveness about six times higher and soil responsiveness about three times higher. Hysteresis analysis further revealed clearer rainfall-dependent switching in lake–river coupling than in groundwater–river coupling, with lake-specific transition thresholds concentrated within a relatively narrow rainfall range of 2.7–4.6 mm, whereas groundwater transitions were weakly constrained or unresolved at most wells. These results indicate that thermokarst lakes do not simply act as permanent water-retaining reservoirs, but instead reorganize the timing and pathways of water transfer, linking stronger event-scale connectivity with contrasting annual water-retention outcomes. This study provides a process-based reference for understanding hydrological regulation in lake-developing alpine permafrost catchments and evaluating future climate-change impacts on water balance in degrading permafrost regions.

title: Threshold responses of runoff-sediment dynamics to hydrological connectivity
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Taoxi Li, Qian Zeng, Yichen Yin, Gang Sun, Ruyi Zheng, Yichun Ma, Jiale Ye, Peiyao Xiao, Yaojun Liu
abstract: Hydrological connectivity plays a critical role in regulating watershed runoff-sediment processes; however, the responses of runoff–sediment processes to hydrological connectivity remain insufficiently understood. This study quantified hydrological structural connectivity (HSC) and hydrological functional connectivity (HFC) using IC (Index of Connectivity) and IHC (Index of Hydrosedimentological Connectivity) indices in the Longyan watershed. A total of 320 erosive rainfall events recorded from 2015 to 2024 were analyzed to investigate threshold responses of runoff-sediment to hydrological connectivity. The results revealed pronounced threshold effects of hydrological connectivity on runoff and sediment responses, with three critical IHC thresholds identified at −1.77, −1.37, and −0.27. These thresholds define four response patterns of runoff-sediment relationship, which exhibit significant differences in runoff-sediment dynamics. The structural-dominated and weak functional-dominated patterns exhibit limited runoff and sediment generation capacities, whereas the strong functional-dominated pattern contributes substantially to both runoff and sediment export. The extreme rainfall-dominated pattern, although accounting for only 3% of events, contributes 50% of total sediment yield, reflecting markedly enhanced sediment transport efficiency. In this context, increasing the response threshold between hydrological connectivity and runoff-sediment processes is an effective approach to mitigating watershed erosion, particularly under extreme rainfall events. These findings deepen the understanding of watershed soil erosion processes from a hydrological connectivity perspective.

title: Perception-enhanced bidirectional attention networks for short-term time series forecasting of water level in cascade reservoir system
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Wei Luo, Yingjia Li, Feng Zhang, Xinpeng Yu, Shiruo Hu, Jianshi Zhao
abstract: Real-time water level forecasting plays a crucial role in the operation of cascade reservoir systems; however, it remains challenging due to data uncertainties and error propagation. Motivated by recent advances in deep learning algorithms, this study proposes an improved Modern Temporal Convolutional Network (ModernTCN) for cascade reservoir water level prediction. We first develop a Multi-Scale Attention Atrous Spatial Pyramid (MSAASP) module by integrating Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) with Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks (SENet). This design enables more effective extraction of temporal features at multiple scales and adaptively reassigns weights to features according to their relative importance. The MSAASP module is then integrated into ModernTCN to construct the Perception-Enhanced Bidirectional Attention Network (PE-BANet). PE-BANet delivers substantial improvements in water level forecasting accuracy by expanding the model’s perceptual field and effectively learning temporospatial patterns. When applied to the Shenxigou–Zhentouba cascade reservoirs in the Dadu River Basin of China, the proposed method demonstrates superior predictive performance. The results show that PE-BANet outperforms transformer-based, MLP-based, RNN-based, and CNN-based models in both forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency. Specifically, for five-minute water level predictions within a one-hour forecasting horizon, PE-BANet achieves an average error of less than 0.15 m in the cascade reservoir system, thereby providing timely and precise information to support real-time operation and decision-making.

title: T-ResUNet: A deep-learning framework for spatiotemporal prediction of granular–fluid dam-break flows
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Cheng-ming Lei, Shun Wang, Xuan Kang, Zheng-yang Su, Wei Wu
abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of the spatiotemporal evolution of dam-break flows involving granular materials and interstitial fluid is essential for effective risk mitigation and emergency planning. In this paper, we introduce a spatiotemporal deep-learning surrogate model, T-ResUNet, for rapid prediction of two-phase dam-break flows triggered by granular column collapse. The proposed framework integrates a ResUNet architecture for spatial feature extraction with a Transformer module for temporal dependency modeling, enabling stable multi-step forecasting of flow dynamics. High-fidelity CFD–DEM simulations under varying granular and water column conditions are used to construct the training dataset. Results show that the model accurately reproduces the evolution of water volume fraction and achieves satisfactory performance in predicting flow velocity across 100 autoregressive steps. The model also demonstrates robust predictive capability for unseen parameter combinations within the training domain and maintains reasonable performance under limited extrapolation scenarios. These results demonstrate that the proposed T-ResUNet framework offers an efficient surrogate modeling strategy for laboratory-scale 2D-vertical granular–fluid dam-break flows. It achieves a favorable trade-off between computational efficiency and predictive accuracy while establishing a methodological foundation for future extensions to more complex fluid–solid coupled scenarios.

title: A bias-corrected deep learning-based data assimilation method for riverine bathymetry inversion
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Runyi Yang, Jiangjiang Zhang, Lei Yao, Hongwu Zhang
abstract: Riverine bathymetry is essential for flood prevention, navigation planning, and ecological management, yet its direct measurements are often costly or impractical. Model-based inversion using readily available observations, such as flow velocity and water surface elevation, offers a promising alternative. Traditional deterministic approaches, however, are sensitive to observational and model errors and cannot fully quantify uncertainties. Within a Bayesian framework, bathymetry inversion can be treated as a stochastic inverse problem, producing more reliable, uncertainty-aware estimates. Ensemble-based methods, including the Kalman-based ensemble smoother (ES(K)) and the deep learning-based ensemble smoother (ES(DL )), provide computationally efficient implementations, with ES(DL) better capturing non-Gaussian features. Both methods, however, may exhibit biases in extreme value predictions. To address this, we propose a simple yet effective bias-correction strategy for ES(DL), resulting in the new EC(DL) method. Comprehensive numerical experiments show that ES(DL) matches ES(K) in Gaussian settings, while EC(DL) slightly outperforms both. In non-Gaussian scenarios involving extreme values, ES(DL) outperforms ES(K), and EC(DL) achieves the best overall performance. The proposed EC(DL) method demonstrates robust performance across diverse noise levels and observation layouts, highlighting its reliability, adaptability, and practical utility in riverine bathymetry inversion.

title: Efficiency of emulsion flooding for the removal of organic pollutants from soils: A pore-scale study on the effects of oil volume fraction, injection flow rate, and wettability
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Shuxin Wang, Antonio Rodriguez de Castro, Fernando Leal-Calderon, Azita Ahmadi-Senichault, Abdelaziz Omari
abstract: Emulsion flooding (EF) is a promising in situ strategy for remediating aquifers contaminated with organic pollutants, yet the pore-scale mechanisms driving its efficiency remain unclear. This study investigates EF at the pore scale using calibrated oil-in-water emulsions in micromodels mimicking pollutant infiltration and removal. The analysis systematically examines how emulsion oil volume fraction ϕ, injection flow rate, and micromodel wettability influence pollutant removal and shape the morphology and connectivity of trapped pollutant ganglia, offering a pore-scale insight largely absent from previous EF investigations. Shear-thinning emulsions with sub-pore droplets achieve ∼ 97% recovery at ϕ = 0.72 by combining piston-like displacement with progressive mobilization and fragmentation of residual blobs, a mechanism not observed in low-viscosity Newtonian emulsions (ϕ ≤ 0.45), which mainly follow water-saturated channels and exhibit poor sweeping efficiency. Wettability strongly influenced recovery by controlling initial pollutant distribution, connectivity, and pore wall coatings; in oil-wet micromodels, highly connected pollutant ganglia restricted the flow of low-concentrated emulsions. During EF, the average size of pollutant-containing pores decreased in water-wet systems, whereas in oil-wet systems, large pollutant islands were eroded with little pore-size selectivity, highlighting the role of pore structure and wettability in optimizing emulsion-based remediation. Residual pollutant blobs aligned mostly perpendicular to flow at maximum recovery, defining a limit for mechanical displacement of the pollutant. Higher injection rates enhanced pollutant mobilization, while excessive emulsion viscosity increased injection pressure, suggesting potential limits for operational feasibility. These findings provide physics-based guidance for optimizing EF operational parameters and underscore its potential for efficient aquifer remediation.

title: Scaling relationships between catchment area and peak discharge across the Fitzroy Basin, eastern Australia
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Jasmine B.D. Jaffrés, Chris Cuff, Cecily E. Rasmussen
abstract: Specific discharge – the flow rate per unit catchment area – highlights the spatial variability of rainfall–runoff events. These events rarely affect entire catchments uniformly, particularly in large river systems such as the Fitzroy Basin in eastern Australia. Using peak historical flow rates from 136 stream gauges, this study evaluates log–log scaling relationships between catchment area and specific discharge across the entire basin and nine major, nested subcatchments. The site-specific historical peaks across such a large and hydrologically diverse basin are used to assess how scaling behaviour varies with operational record length, rainfall extent and subcatchment characteristics. Peak specific discharge exhibits a strong inverse relationship with catchment area, consistent with power-law scaling. However, this relationship is more robust for gauges with longer operational records. Short operational periods reduce the likelihood of capturing rare, high-magnitude flow events and can substantially weaken scaling regressions. The analysis identifies specific gauges that exert disproportionate influence on the fitted exponents, offering practical guidance for gauge selection in future scaling and flood-frequency studies. Accurate estimation of extreme flows is further complicated by highly complex, non-stationary riverbed cross-sections, with some floodplains spanning several kilometres, reducing the reliability of rating curves during major floods. Improved characterisation of peak specific discharge enhances the predictive capacity for extreme flow rates, particularly under projected increases in atmospheric moisture that are likely to amplify peak flows during extreme rainfall events.

title: Weight-optimized fusion of satellite precipitation over the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau: Comparison of machine learning approaches
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Li Zhou, Chun Zhou, Zhongshun Gu, Yinan Guo, Ting Chen, Xiaojun Guo, Juan Du, Jiajia Yue, Keying Liu, Lingling Wu, Jingyuan Xue
abstract: Precipitation estimation over the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) is challenging due to strong spatial heterogeneity under climate change. Using ground observations as reference, we fused the Global Satellite Mapping of Precipitation (GSMaP) and the Integrated Multi-satellite Retrievals for the Global Precipitation Measurement mission (IMERG) products with auxiliary predictors (Digital Elevation Model (DEM), soil moisture, and land surface temperature) to develop four widely used machine-learning fusion models (Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Transformer), and further incorporated an intensity- and error-adaptive weighted mean squared error (WMSE) loss into all four fusion models as an explicit sample-reweighting strategy. The results demonstrate that WMSE-based weighting generally improved fusion performance relative to both the original satellite products and the corresponding unweighted baselines, with the most consistent gains appearing in precipitation-event detection. For RF, LSTM, and Transformer, POD increased by 13.8–30.0% and CSI by 12.1–19.1%, while FAR decreased by 1.5–3.2%. The improvement was rainfall-intensity dependent, with the most stable gains occurring for light-to-moderate precipitation, whereas stronger rainfall showed larger model-dependent variability associated with sample scarcity and the POD-FAR trade-off. Across elevation bands, the fusion models remained robust, and WMSE helped mitigate underestimation at high elevations. In addition, the weighted fusion models better reproduced the southeast–northwest precipitation gradient across the QTP than the satellite-only estimates. Overall, the WMSE-based fusion framework provides a practical strategy for precipitation estimation over complex high-altitude terrain.

title: Combining multiple groundwater hydrograph analyses to characterize aquifer dynamics and drivers in complex hydrogeological settings
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Z. Chai, N.K. LeRoux, R.C. Jamieson, A.M.R. Hill, L.D. Somers, B.L. Kurylyk
abstract: Groundwater level fluctuations reveal key aspects of aquifer behavior, including recharge timing, storage dynamics, and sensitivity to hydroclimatic forcing. However, in geologically heterogeneous and seasonally variable regions, interpreting these fluctuations remains challenging, and we lack standard approaches for characterizing aquifers based on groundwater hydrographs. In this study, we analyzed 13 years (2011–2023) of daily groundwater level data from 40 provincial observation wells across Nova Scotia, Canada, to characterize spatial and temporal groundwater dynamics. We extracted 17 hydrograph-derived indices for characterizing the hydrographs and aquifers and apply time series decomposition to quantify the magnitude, frequency, and timing of groundwater fluctuations. Most wells exhibited consistent seasonal patterns, with a median annual level range of 0.7 m and a dominant periodicity near 365 days. Seasonal components accounted for an average of 54% of the total variance and were the primary mode of variability in 80% of wells. The timing of annual groundwater maxima clustered in either spring or autumn–winter, depending on whether recharge was predominantly snowmelt- or rainfall-driven. Hydrograph clustering revealed four behavioral groups linked to differences in geology, depth, and precipitation responsiveness. Recharge estimation using the water table fluctuation method was applied to 14 seasonally dynamic wells, yielding mean annual recharge rates of 180–250 mm/year. Winter/early-spring recharge (January–April) accounted for 40% of annual recharge but only 32% of annual precipitation, indicating higher cold-season recharge efficiency. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of hydrograph-based analysis for understanding aquifer function and seasonal recharge dynamics across complex hydrogeological settings with changing snow-rain partitioning.

title: Climatic drying-wetting cycles induced dynamic coupling effect between 3D soil desiccation cracking and moisture redistribution
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Yu-Xuan Chen, Jun-Zheng Zhang, Chao-Sheng Tang, Run-Yang Lan, Qing Cheng, Jin-jian Xu, Ben-Gang Tian
abstract: Desiccation cracking in clayey soils is a common natural phenomenon. The mechanical and hydraulic properties of cracked soil are sensitive to drying and wetting events, causing various geotechnical and environmental problems. This study characterizes the three-dimensional evolution of cracking morphology and moisture distribution of in-situ clayey soils. The soils were exposed to natural drying and to simulated rainfall events that replicated historical climate extremes. Electrical resistivity tomography was applied to monitor a 0.5 × 0.5 m clayey soil site with a desiccation cracking network during multiple drought and rainfall events. Laboratory measurements established the quantitative relationship between soil electrical resistivity and gravimetric moisture content. The resistivity tomograms successfully characterized the 3D desiccation-cracking network, including cracks that were invisible at the soil surface. Differences in resistivity evolution between soil near and away from cracks indicate that soil with closed cracks exhibits greater dynamic moisture changes and a heightened response to drying-wetting cycles. Results reveal a coupling effect between crack morphology dynamics and moisture distribution, in which the desiccation crack served as a preferential pathway for both evaporation and infiltration, while moisture localization around the crack can cause its closure. The resistivity model, combined with multi-source data, reconstructs the evolution of crack morphology and moisture distribution during drying-wetting cycles, providing crucial information for assessing soil and slope integrity.

title: Physics-informed extreme learning machine with time-marching and random features for unsaturated groundwater flow
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Biao Yuan, Roberto Cudmani, Wei Yan, He Yang, Ana Heitor, Yanjie Song, Xiaohui Chen
abstract: Machine learning (ML) offers new opportunities for numerical modeling in engineering, yet purely data-driven approaches require large datasets and lack physical interpretability, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often have high computational costs due to their gradient-based optimization. This study presents a Physics-Informed Extreme Learning Machine (PIELM) based on Time-Marching Strategy and Random Feature Method (TMS-RFM) to efficiently solve highly nonlinear unsaturated groundwater flow problems, namely TR-PIELM. Built upon shallow neural networks and physics-informed machine learning (PIML), TR-PIELM encodes the governing equations and initial-boundary conditions of unsaturated infiltration into the loss function, enabling both soft-constraint learning and hard boundary enforcement. Benchmark tests include 1D steady/transient flows, two-layer soil infiltration, coupled unsaturated infiltration and deformation, slope stability analysis, and 2D transient flows, demonstrating that TR-PIELM accurately captures pressure head dynamics. The results are compared with analytical or finite difference solutions. Quantitatively, TR-PIELM achieves up to 10 10 -fold reduction in relative L 2 error compared with PINNs for steady problem and 10 2 -fold reduction for transient problems, and attains accuracy comparable or even better than fourth-order Runge–Kutta (RK4) schemes while requiring significantly less computational time. Furthermore, the effects of key factors influencing model performance and potential improvement directions are discussed. This study highlights the method’s applicability to highly nonlinear PDEs in engineering, offering a fast, reliable, and scalable framework for simulating unsaturated seepage.

title: A soil freezing characteristic model considering the tortuous structure and complex distribution of soil pores
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Jianyuan Zhao, Shuangyang Li, Qi Jiang, Minqi Dong, Chun Bao, Shangqi Zhou, Huiyin Liu
abstract: Unfrozen water content (UWC) significantly affects the hydro-thermo-mechanical behaviors of frozen soils and further affects hydrological processes and stability of engineering in cold regions. The UWC is strongly temperature-dependent and described by a soil freezing characteristic curve (SFCC), a fundamental hydraulic property of frozen soils. Numerous SFCC models have been established based on capillary theory, thermodynamic theories. However, most existing models idealize soil pores as bundles of cylindrical capillaries (BCC), which cannot adequately represent the tortuous pore geometry of natural soils, and the corresponding pore size distribution is often difficult to obtain experimentally. To address these limitations, a theoretical SFCC model, termed SFCC-FCPD, is developed by characterizing soil pores as fractal capillaries (FC) and deriving the cumulative pore distribution (PD) from the probability distribution of soil particles. The robustness of the SFCC-FCPD model was verified against measured data. The predicted results show good agreement with observations, with coefficients of determination R2 exceeding 0.95. In the SFCC-FCPD model, the cumulative distribution of pores is directly obtained from the probability distribution of soil particles, which avoids the time-consuming and laborious experiments. Moreover, the fractal theory is used to characterize irregular pore shapes, which makes the theoretical capillary close to the actual pore structures. Therefore, the SFCC-FCPD model exhibits excellent ability of predicting the UWC change in freezing soils, offering a critical insight into hydraulic characteristics in frozen soils as well as providing a key tool for the studying of hydrological, agricultural, engineering, and environmental studies in cold regions.

title: Impact of fractal dimensions of rainfall time series on mountain flood forecasting
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Zhixu Bai, Fangqing Jiang, Ruonan Hao, Yue-Ping Xu, Jiayi Fang
abstract: Rainfall in mountainous watersheds is characterized by strong spatial and temporal heterogeneity, which poses a great challenge to flood forecasting. Time series of rainfall and water level, as reflections of natural processes, follow fractal theory with self-similarity in their fluctuations and variations. However, the impact of fractal properties in rainfall time series on minute-scale flood forecasting has been overlooked. In this study, the rainfall series from 17 rainfall gauges and one water level station within a 339-km2 watershed were used to reveal the fractal dimensions ( D ) of rainfall and water level series and the impact on flood forecasting. The results show that a fractal relationship existed between rainfall and water level across time scales, with 5.33 h as the division point between short-term and medium-term time scales. Within this scale, the model showed excellent forecasting performance. The fractal dimension of rainfall time series was significantly correlated with model forecasting accuracy, for both water level and peak time. When the spatial uniformity of rainfall gauges exceeded a threshold, further improving uniformity could not enhance the fractal dimension of the rainfall time series. This study confirmed that combining rainfall fractal dimension with rainfall gauge evaluation indicators could support mountainous rainfall gauge network planning and flood prediction.

title: Including water-salinity stress hysteresis and compensation to empirical root water uptake models
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Yanqi Xu, Wanzi Hu, Qiang Zuo, Jianchu Shi, Yuchun Fan, Xun Wu, Alon Ben-Gal
abstract: Root water uptake (RWU) is influenced not only by instantaneous soil conditions but also by two dynamic processes often neglected in models: stress hysteresis, arising from prior exposure to suboptimal water/salinity conditions, and compensation, whereby roots in favorable zones offset reduced uptake in zones less conducive to RWU. Empirical RWU models, such as the Feddes model (FM), are widely used but typically neglect these dynamic effects. Here, we extended FM by introducing a recovery coefficient to capture stress hysteresis and incorporating either a piecewise or continuous compensation function. Six models were tested: FM, single-process models WM (hysteresis), PM (piecewise compensation), and DM (continuous compensation); and combined-process models − WM-PM and WM-DM. Using data from a greenhouse soil column experiment with winter wheat, we found that both historical stress and spatial heterogeneity in root zone water and salinity strongly influence RWU and transpiration by plants. The coupled models (WM-PM, WM-DM) outperformed FM and single-process models in simulating transpiration dynamics, improving R 2 by 10.1–12.9% and 3.8–29.7% for actual and relative transpiration, while reducing RMSE by 27.6–36.4% and 13.8–41.9%, respectively. The WM-DM showed the highest accuracy attributed to its compensation function incorporating soil hydraulic conductivity, matric potential, and osmotic potential. Coupled with the one-dimensional Richards and convection–dispersion equations, WM-DM successfully reproduced soil water and salinity dynamics in greenhouse soil column experiment and a two-year field study of a winter wheat–summer maize rotation. In addition, model robustness analysis showed that WM-DM exhibited limited sensitivity to most parameters, lower uncertainties for the salinity and recovery stress response parameters than for the water-deficit and compensation stress response parameters, and unavoidable parameter non-uniqueness under simultaneous optimization. These findings highlight the value of accounting for both stress hysteresis and compensation in empirical RWU models for improved irrigation scheduling and salinity management.

title: Quantitative attribution of seasonal runoff variations in the Yellow River Basin under unsteady conditions using a modified Budyko framework
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Junjie Wang, Yuning Chi, Shaoxiong Zhang, Bing Shi, Liting Zhang, Chenjun Du, Xin Li, Baoqi Li, Liqin Yang, Lei Huang, Dian Yuan, Kaiyang Qiu, Panxing He
abstract: The changes in climate and watershed properties are reshaping hydrological processes worldwide at multiple scales, leading to a transition from steady to non-stationary states. The traditional Budyko framework commonly relies on a steady-state assumption and neglects terrestrial water storage changes, thereby exhibiting notable limitations at finer temporal scales. Hence, a novel runoff elasticity attribution model was developed by integrating a modified Budyko framework (incorporating parameter λ for watershed properties and y0 for the net effect of terrestrial water storage dynamics), Random Forest, and a CNN-LSTM-Attention neural network. Then, the spatial differences in seasonal runoff variations were revealed by the proposed runoff elasticity attribution model in the Yellow River Basin during 1960–2020. The results show that the CNN-LSTM-Attention model can effectively interpret the parameters λ and y0, with determination coefficients (R2) exceeding 0.9 between simulated and calibrated values. Precipitation and terrestrial water storage exert positive controlling effects on runoff, whereas potential evapotranspiration and underlying surface changes suppress runoff generation. In the source region of the Yellow River Basin, climatic factors (precipitation and potential evapotranspiration) contribute 33.9% to the overall runoff variation. The influence of underlying surface changes on runoff gradually increases along the downstream direction, accounting for 68.6%, 80.0%, and 87.6% of the variation in the upper, middle, and lower reaches, respectively. Seasonal runoff in arid regions shows greater sensitivity to the net effect of terrestrial water storage dynamics, accounting for 9.0% of the runoff variation in the upper Yellow River. A new methodological framework is provided in this study for diagnostic attribution and adaptive management of watershed water resources under evolving environmental conditions.

title: Quantifying hydrological acceleration: A process-based framework and its application in arid regions
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Xingming Hao, Jingjing Zhang, Mengtao Ci, Fan Sun, Qixiang Liang, Jinfan Xu, Xue Fan
abstract: Global warming is accelerating the global hydrological cycle, yet current assessments remain constrained by static water-balance methods that overlook dynamic flux rates and yield fragmented insights. To address this gap, we propose a novel rate of hydrological change (RHC) index that systematically quantifies hydrological acceleration in arid inland river basins of Northwest China. By integrating multi-source observations, models, and reanalysis data, our method provides a unified perspective on the coupled atmosphere-to-runoff system, including water-phase changes. Results demonstrated a consistent acceleration of the regional water cycle. Process-based variables, including glacial mass loss (+58.36%) and evapotranspiration (+26.83%), exhibited more pronounced increases than state variables, reflecting a stronger response of phase-change processes within the accelerated hydrological cycle. The spatially weighted hydrological change rates reached 22.58% based on state variables (RHCs) and 25.61% based on process metrics (RHCp), with clear spatial gradients observed across mountain systems. Glacial melt and precipitation‐to‐runoff conversion were identified as the primary drivers of acceleration. Large‐scale climate forcings, particularly atmospheric circulation patterns and ocean–atmosphere interactions, dominated hydrological variability, accounting for 73% to 80% of the explained variance, significantly surpassing the influence of local climate factors and human activities. Causal loop analysis further revealed bidirectional feedback mechanisms between water cycle acceleration and drought subsystems, showing that intensification of process variables amplified meteorological drought while buffering hydrological drought. Our study provides a systematic and mechanism-based perspective on hydrological cycle intensification in arid regions. The RHC framework offers a transferable approach to diagnosing complex hydrological responses to climate change, underscoring the need for process-based metrics in future water resource vulnerability assessments.

title: Irrigation enhanced nitrification and hydrological partitioning drive groundwater nitrate accumulation in an agricultural irrigation district
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Xu Yang, Ruihong Yu, Guanglei Yu, Yansong Bai, Shen Qu, Dong Qian, Muhan Li, Zeyuan Liu, Ping Miao, Hongli Ma
abstract: Nitrate (NO3 −) contamination in irrigation dominated agricultural regions poses a persistent threat to groundwater quality, yet the distribution patterns and underlying mechanisms of NO3 − among hydrologically connected water bodies in irrigation districts remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated a large Yellow River irrigation district using multi-season field sampling combined with nitrate dual isotopes (δ15N–NO3 −, δ18O–NO3 −), water stable isotopes (δ2H–δ18O), 222Rn tracers, dissolved organic matter fluorescence, Bayesian isotope mixing models, and soil microbial functional gene analyses. Across all seasons, NO3 − was the dominant inorganic nitrogen species, with shallow groundwater exhibiting persistent enrichment, which were 3.1–4.8 times higher than those in canals, drainage and Yellow River water. Isotopic evidence and source apportionment revealed manure and sewage as the dominant anthropogenic nitrogen sources, while δ18O–NO3 − signatures and increased (AOA + AOB)/(nirS + nirK) ratios demonstrated that irrigation significantly enhanced soil nitrification. Concurrent enrichment of groundwater δ2H–δ18O and elevated 222Rn activities indicated intensified shallow recharge during irrigation, promoting downward NO3 − transfer into the aquifer. In contrast, drainage exhibited low NO3 − concentrations (1.74 ± 0.90 mg L−1) due to strong dilution and short residence times, despite receiving substantial anthropogenic nitrogen inputs (manure and sewage contributed 65.7%). These results demonstrate that irrigation enhanced nitrification and hydrological partitioning jointly control NO3 − fate. Our findings identify shallow aquifers as long term NO3 − reservoirs in irrigation system and underscore the need to incorporate groundwater retention processes into NO3 − risk assessment and management.

title: Reconstruction of soil moisture time series with characterisation of drydown attributes
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Jhilam Sinha, Ashish Sharma, Lucy Marshall
abstract: Encapsulating soil water drying attributes in derived remote sensing products is essential for their application to various environmental studies. Systematic differences are observed for soil moisture (SM) drying phases (drydown) in Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) level 4 (SMAP L4) product when compared to ground observations due to differences in measurement processes. An algorithm (BRF: Bivariate Recursive Filter) is able to translate drydown parameters, namely the drydown recession coefficient and initial wetness, to in-situ scale to enhance consistency with regional in-situ observations. Here, we propose a reconstruction procedure to structure the complete SM time series so that it is compatible with the bivariate transformed drydown attributes. The present study develops the reconstructed SM time series at any grid location SMAP L4 data is available at. The method is validated with 6 global in-situ networks and improvements have been observed in the reconstructed SMAP SM series. Significant enhancements are observed particularly during the drydown periods. Additional improvement is noticed when observations from spatially nearby in-situ stations for a target grid is used; this can assist in regional hydrological studies whenever ground data is available.

title: Characterizing the distribution and flow dynamics of shallow karst fissure-type groundwater in urban environments using multi-geophysical time-lapse monitoring combined with saline tracer tests
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Hao Sun, Tao Hu, Fangyuan Dai, Jingxin Wu, Xiujun Guo, Shixin Yan, Xiao Shi, Tianyuan Zheng
abstract: Approximately 1.18 billion people inhabit karst regions globally. Rapid urbanization exacerbates the mutual feedback and conflicts between underground infrastructure and shallow karst groundwater. Characterizing its distribution and flow dynamics is a prerequisite for understanding these interactions and implementing effective hazard mitigation. However, delineating the hydrodynamics of shallow fissure-type karst systems typical of northern China is highly challenging due to the absence of large connected conduits, complex infillings, profound heterogeneity, and restricted urban exploration space. To address this, we propose an integrated methodology combining saline-enhanced time-lapse Borehole-Surface Electrical Resistivity Tomography (BSERT), Self-Potential (SP), the Mise-à-la-Masse (MALM) method, geological drilling, and tracer tests, validated in Jinan, China. At the local scale, this method effectively characterizes the spatial distribution and hydraulic connectivity of shallow karst aquifers, capturing the non-linear opening and closing dynamics of karst channels driven by local hydraulic pressure. At the regional scale, it qualitatively identifies the preferential flow directions of the shallow runoff zone. Based on these findings, we established a classification system of eight typical occurrence patterns, clarifying the spatiotemporal allocation mechanisms of Recharge-Storage-Flow (R-S-F). This work provides a theoretical reference for conceptualizing and numerically modeling complex karst systems, offering crucial technical support for formulating differentiated strategies for engineering hazard prevention and groundwater protection in restricted urban environments.

title: High-Precision baseflow separation in data-scarce regions with machine learning models
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Rong Zhong, Hang Lyu, Xiaosi Su, Tingting Deng, Aimin Cai, Yanxi Wu, Jingzun Mao, Peng Zhou
abstract: Accurate baseflow separation is vital for ecological conservation, hydrological model validation, and water resource management. However, the application of electrical conductivity (EC)-based methods is often constrained by the lack of daily EC observations in many basins, which limits the accuracy of baseflow estimation. To address this challenge, we reconstructed daily EC from sparse measurements using machine-learning models and commonly available hydroclimatic and basin data. Using data from 147 monitoring sites in the Colorado and Missouri River basins, which span contrasting climatic and basin conditions, we evaluated EC regression models across ecoregions under simulated data-scarce conditions. Weekly and monthly subsampling schemes were used to represent limited monitoring frequency, and support vector regression, decision tree, random forest (RF), and a conventional power-law function were compared. The results showed that RF achieved the highest accuracy, outperforming the power-law function by 24%, and that model performance varied systematically across five ecoregions according to key hydroclimatic and basin controls. The accuracy of the optimal regression model relied on the quality of the training set, particularly the negative streamflow-EC correlation, and we observed that correlation coefficients below −0.4 ensured more reliable results. To minimize costs in regions with limited conductivity data, our results suggest that monitoring EC about 156 times at weekly intervals over three years or 182 times at monthly intervals over 15 years can meet the RF model’s data requirements. These findings offer guidance for EC monitoring design and enable more reliable CMB-based baseflow separation in data-scarce regions.

title: Temporal scale dictates the dominant driver of lake dynamics on the Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 675 Author(s): Ting Li, Yuanwei Wang, Lingxiao Wang, Lei Wang, Jing Zhou, Xiaoyu Guo, Jie Xu, Chenhao Chai, Zhaoyan Xie, Sichen Lin, Shiqi Ao, Xingjiao Zhang, Lin Zhao
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau (TP), widely known as the “Third Pole” and “Asian Water Tower”, hosts lakes that act as crucial indicators of climate change. While most TP lakes have expanded significantly in recent decades, gaps in high-temporal-resolution data and unclear scale-dependent driving mechanisms remain. Focusing on inner TP (ITP) lakes during 1972–2021, we used the self-attention-based imputation for time series (SAITS) deep-learning model to fill remote-sensing data gaps, Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to quantify factor contributions, and the Mann‒Kendall test to detect trend breakpoints. Results show the total ITP lake area increased from 2.69 × 104 to 3.66 × 104 km2 (36% growth) over 50 years: it remained relatively stable in 1972–1995, and entered a phase of marked expansion from 1996 (a breakpoint for annual mean area identified by Mann‒Kendall test), and slowed after 2006 (a 2006 breakpoint for October area). Two large lakes—Selin Co and Ayakkum Lake—saw the largest area increases, exceeding 300 km2 (+738 km2 and + 520 km2 respectively). A total of 433 new lakes formed over the period, with a combined area of 1255 km2 (accounting for 12.4% of total ITP lake expansion), mostly concentrated in northern ITP. Notably, temporal scale dictates the dominant drivers of lake dynamics: subsurface runoff dominates at the monthly scale (with positive SHAP contributions when subsurface runoff > 10 mm), while energy factors (e.g., downward surface thermal radiation) are the primary drivers at the annual scale. This study clarifies the multi-scale mechanisms of ITP lake dynamics, providing robust data support for regional water resource management.

title: Hydrogeochemical constraints on the genesis, fluid mixing, and heavy metal mobilization of low-temperature geothermal systems in the Mufushan granite batholith, South China
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Linxin Li, Zhengqing Wu, Lei Wang, Jian Ou, Jing Pi, Sheng Liu, Lala Wei, Liuqin Huang, Hongchen Jiang, Yanlong Dong
abstract: Understanding the genetic mechanisms, fluid mixing processes, and environmental risks associated with heavy metal mobilization within geothermal systems is essential for optimizing their safe and sustainable utilization, particularly within stable continental blocks such as South China's Mufushan area. This study employs hydrochemical analysis, isotope tracing (δD-δ18O and 87Sr/86Sr ratios), and thermodynamic modeling to investigate the Mufushan geothermal system in Hunan Province. Results reveal that the geothermal waters predominantly belong to the Na-HCO3 hydrochemical type, with temperatures ranging from 36.0°C to 51.9°C and pH values between 7.98 and 9.34, indicating weak alkalinity. The enrichment of lithium, fluoride, and silica is primarily attributable to the dissolution of granitic pegmatites, with atmospheric precipitation serving as the main recharge source. The analysis of the Na-K-Mg ternary diagram and cation exchange indices suggests that the geothermal waters have not yet reached water-rock equilibrium and are significantly affected by mixing with meteoric water. Hydrochemical characteristics are jointly governed by silicate weathering, strong cation exchange processes, likely related to Yanshanian granitic pegmatites intrusions in the region. Silica geothermometry estimates reservoir temperatures between approximately 109.6°C and 128.4°C at depths of 2772.41 to 3415.58 meters. Elevated concentrations of heavy metals, including lithium, arsenic, chromium, copper, manganese, and zinc, which are linked to pegmatite leaching processes. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the genetic evolution of the Mufushan geothermal system and underscores the importance of addressing heavy metal contamination risks in future resource exploitation.

title: Properties of the mid-deep ground source heat pump system with borehole heat exchangers direct heating loop
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Shilong Yang, Guangxin Zhang, Yaru Li, Qingbo Yang, Ke Zhu, Yudong Mao, Wenke Zhang, Mingzhi Yu
abstract: This study proposes a direct-heating mid-deep ground source heat pump system (DH-MGSHPS) with switchable parallel and series arrangements of mid-deep borehole heat exchangers (MBHEs). A distinguishing feature of the investigated configuration is the inclusion of switchable parallel and series arrangements for the MBHEs, which is intended to extend the duration of direct heating under varying load conditions. Based on a dynamic simulation platform developed by coupling a self-developed MBHE heat-transfer model with TRNSYS, the long-term operating characteristics of the DH-MGSHPS are evaluated under hourly building heating loads. An orthogonal experimental design is employed to quantify the influence of key geological and design parameters on direct-heating duration. The results show that the proposed switching strategy can effectively extend the duration of direct heating and reduce heat-pump operation, resulting in improved system performance compared with a conventional mid-deep ground source heat pump system (MGSHPS). Although the direct-heating duration gradually decreases due to long-term ground temperature decline, the system maintains a measurable energy-saving effect over 20 years. The sensitivity analysis indicates that terrestrial heat flow is the dominant factor affecting direct-heating duration, followed by borehole depth and pipe dimensions. The findings suggest that the DH-MGSHPS with flexible MBHE arrangements represents a viable approach for improving the long-term performance of MGSHPS, particularly in regions with favorable geothermal conditions.

title: Field-validated thermo-mechanical behavior of energy pile groups in high-altitude regions
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Hanlin Lu, Chenglong Wang, Abdelmalek Bouazza, Xuanming Ding, Qiang Ou, Xiaochuan Hu, Gangqiang Kong
abstract: The low ground temperature and strong confinement of thick, coarse-grained strata significantly modify the heat transfer and thermo-mechanical behavior of energy piles in high-altitude regions, yet in situ evidence remains limited. This study addresses this gap through full-scale field testing of an energy pile within a rigidly capped pile group at a ∼3500 m plateau site, supported by three-dimensional sequential thermo-mechanical finite element modelling. The active pile was subjected to 120 h of continuous heating and cooling under constant vertical load, with temperature and strain monitored along the pile length. Results show pronounced thermal asymmetry. Heating-induced temperature increases occur along the entire pile, whereas cooling produces negligible changes below ∼11 m, indicating limited heat-extraction capacity at depth. Combined cap and soil constraints strongly restrained free thermal deformation, leading to depth-dependent stress accumulation and non-uniform responses. Thermal interaction within the pile group was weak, with adjacent piles responding mainly through passive, cap-controlled deformation. These findings provide field-validated guidance for optimizing pipe layout and operational strategies of energy piles in cold, high-altitude environments.

title: Possibilities and limitations of two-phase flow CFD modelling for geothermal applications: A literature review
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Vijay Chauhan, Brandon Velasquez, Gudrun Saevarsdottir, Maria Gudjonsdottir
abstract: A conventional geothermal system often involves fluid flow in a two-phase state across its various components. Current methods for two-phase flow analysis in the geothermal industry predominantly rely on system codes to determine bulk fluid flow characteristics. However, recent developments in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) modelling for various industrial applications involving two-phase flow present a strong opportunity for its use in the design and analysis of geothermal processes. Applying CFD can aid in understanding and optimizing overall geothermal utilization and its components to achieve an efficient, cost-optimal solution. This work discusses the state-of-the-art in two-phase CFD modelling applicable to geothermal processes. Case studies from the literature regarding the two-phase CFD modelling of geothermal operations, along with other relevant studies, are presented. This review aims to assist engineers and researchers by highlighting the applicability of different two-phase CFD models for specific geothermal processes based on their unique flow characteristics. Additionally, it discusses various CFD models applied by other industries that share a similar scope with the geothermal sector. Limitations and challenges inherent in the computational modelling of geothermal processes are also addressed. Ultimately, this study focuses on reviewing the application of CFD for modelling two-phase flow in geothermal systems, specifically involving gas-liquid and solid-gas phases.

title: Experimental study on the propagation of double flaws in granite after high temperature cycling under biaxial conditions
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Tian Sun, Benguo He, Binglei Li
abstract: In deep underground engineering and energy development, rock masses containing flaws are frequently subjected to cyclic high-temperature (CHT) treatments and complex stress conditions, making their mechanical behavior and failure mechanisms a topic of considerable concern. To reveal the damage and crack evolution characteristics of thermally cycled flawed granite, this study conducted biaxial compression (BC) tests on samples with different flaw inclination angles (α) under room temperature (RT) and various CHT conditions. The results demonstrate that both CHT and α exert a significant influence on the mechanical failure behavior of flawed granite. CHT400 °C markedly enhances the strength and characteristic stress thresholds, whereas CHT600 °C leads to pronounced weakening. Samples with α = 0° consistently exhibit higher strength, and the effect of α on strength varies with temperature. Under CHT400 °C, cumulative AE hits and energy increase significantly with α, with the α = 90° samples showing stronger low-frequency characteristics. Notably, thermally induced macrocracks are predominantly observed in samples subjected to CHT600 °C with α = 0° and 30° (i.e., small α), and only under such conditions do the two flaws jointly dominate the crack propagation paths and failure modes. Moreover, failure is primarily governed by tensile cracks, while shear mechanisms are markedly enhanced in the later loading stages and become particularly pronounced when α ≥ 45°

title: Optimizing three-dimensional magnetotelluric modeling for geothermal exploration in Al-Lith, western Saudi Arabia
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Abdul Latif Ashadi, Bülent Tezkan, Pritam Yogeshwar, Panagiotis Kirmizakis, Tilman Hanstein, Pantelis Soupios
abstract: The Al-Lith area in western Saudi Arabia is one of the most promising geothermal provinces, as indicated by active surface manifestations such as hot springs. To investigate the subsurface structure and geothermal potential, a broadband magnetotelluric (MT) survey was conducted at 50 stations with periods ranging from 0.001 to 512 s, complemented by transient electromagnetic (TEM) soundings at selected sites. The shallow resistivity structure derived from TEM data was incorporated as a priori information to optimize the 3D MT result. The final 3D resistivity model images a geothermal system comprising a deep conductive reservoir, convective upflow zones, and a fractured aquifer system. The model reveals a conductive body (< 20 Ωm) below ∼2.5 km depth, interpreted as the main geothermal reservoir. Although the structure persists to greater depths (∼8 km) in the inversion, sensitivity analyses indicate that resolution decreases with depth, and thus its deeper extent remains less constrained. Several narrow conductive protrusions rising from the reservoir toward the surface are interpreted as preferential fluid pathways that enable geothermal convection. These pathways are consistent with the surface geothermal expression observed in Al-Lith, which is locally manifested as an active hot spring. Sensitivity tests conducted for each conductive protrusion confirm their robustness. This study presents the first fully 3D geoelectric model of the Al-Lith geothermal system, offering a robust basis for future exploration drilling, resource estimation, and feasibility assessment of geothermal energy utilization in Saudi Arabia.

title: Numerical simulation of thermal plume propagation in shallow aquifers: A case study from Kütahya (Türkiye)
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Ali Samet Öngen, Zeynal Abiddin Ergüler
abstract: The intensive consumption of fossil fuels, the worsening of global warming, and environmental problems have led countries and researchers to explore renewable energy sources. Shallow geothermal systems make an important contribution to sustainable heating and cooling in urban areas. However, system design may lead to thermal interaction and long-term degradation of aquifer thermal conditions. This study investigates the long-term evolution of thermal plumes generated by shallow geothermal systems in the alluvial aquifer underlying the Kütahya city center. A three-dimensional coupled groundwater flow and heat transport model was developed in FEFLOW to simulate thermal plume development under different hydraulic conductivities (5.1–44.42 m day−1) and system operating flow rate scenarios over a 50-year simulation period. Model results show that hydraulic conductivity and pumping rate strongly control the spatial development of the thermal plume and the extent of the thermal influence zone. Under high hydraulic conductivity conditions (44.42 m day−1), the thermal plume migrated predominantly along the groundwater flow direction without reaching the abstraction well, indicating stable long-term system performance. Low hydraulic conductivity scenarios (≤10 m day−1) resulted in thermal accumulation near the wells and increased risk of thermal breakthrough. The results provide a quantitative evaluation of the hydrogeological controls governing thermal plume evolution in shallow aquifers, offering new insights into long-term heat transport processes and supporting the sustainable design of groundwater heat pump systems.

title: Compression-shear fracture in thermally treated granite: Multiparameter acoustic emission evidence for power-law behavior and critical evolution
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Baojun Chen, Xiaofei Liu, Xiaoran Wang, Qiang Sun, Boyuan Yu, Qiming Zhang, Jinhua Wang, Shuxin Liu, Xin Zhou
abstract: In deep geothermal and underground engineering, instability of high-temperature rock masses is often governed by shear-dominated failure. To investigate the damage evolution and instability mechanisms of thermally damaged granite, compression–shear experiments were conducted on specimens heated to 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C, and 600 °C, with synchronous acoustic emission (AE) and digital image correlation (DIC) monitoring. Rather than relying on single AE intensity measures, the fracture process was analyzed from complementary temporal, spatial, and energetic perspectives using fractal statistics, b-value evolution, and Benioff strain energy scaling. The results show that increasing temperature significantly modifies the organization of microcrack activity, leading to reduced temporal persistence, enhanced spatial dispersion of fracture-related events, and a progressive redistribution of released energy toward lower-magnitude events. The temporal fractal dimension exhibits a clear decline prior to failure, marking the transition of damage evolution into a critical state, while spatial fractal characteristics reflect the development of a more diffuse and complex fracture network under thermal damage. Benioff strain energy accumulation exhibits power-law acceleration as instability approaches. The fitted exponent mf decreases with increasing temperature, indicating reduced energy-release rates and weaker microcrack cooperativity. The onset of the pre-failure rise in mf(t) occurs earlier at higher temperatures, reflecting thermally damaged crack activation and earlier approach to critical instability. These findings provide a coherent interpretation of compression–shear instability in thermally damaged granite and offer a multi-dimensional basis for the interpretation of AE-based monitoring indicators in high-temperature rock engineering applications.

title: Insights on the heterogeneity of thermal transfer in the chalk aquifer using fibre-optic distributed temperature sensing
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Katerina Kyrkou, Joseph Kelly, Adam Booth, Fleur Loveridge, David Boon, Edward Hough, Lawrence Scott, Matthew Jackson, Adrian Butler, Daniel Perez, Athena Chalari
abstract: The design of ground-source heat pump systems depends on reliable determination of heat transport parameters, especially the ground thermal conductivity. An effective thermal conductivity, λeff, is traditionally calculated from in-situ thermal response testing (TRT), expressed as a bulk value for the depth range being tested. However, this practice is insensitive to heterogeneous heat transport within the ground, and flowing groundwater may significantly increase λeff. To characterise high- and/or heterogeneous-flow regimes, e.g. in fractured aquifers, distributed TRT observations are advantageous. Distributed TRTs using fibre-optic distributed temperature sensing (FO-DTS) have therefore been applied at a chalk site (Berkshire, southern UK) to assess heat flow and the depth variability of effective thermal conductivity and flow conditions, within boreholes reaching up to 100 m depth. With a vertical resolution of 0.5 m, FO-DTS can isolate different thermo-hydrogeological conditions in the chalk and particularly the groundwater flow horizons. Values of λeff, measured during a 3-day TRT, vary with depth between 5 and 30 W/m K, compared to thermal conductivities of 2.3–2.9 W/m K measured on chalk core samples. Zones of enhanced λeff correlate with highly permeable flow zones in the aquifer. However, when evaluated during a 7-day cooling phase, λeff is reduced by between 10–60% compared to values measured during heating, highlighting the potential influence of complex convection effects and vertical flow within the open borehole. Overall, this study illustrates the value of distributed spatial assessments of thermo-hydrogeological conditions, and the necessity of combining different testing approaches to characterise heat flow in dual-porosity aquifers.

title: A state-of-the-art review of backfill materials and their influence on ground heat exchanger efficiency in geothermal heat pump systems
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Khaled Salhein, C.J. Kobus, Abdulgani Albagul, Edrees Yahya Alhawsawi, Mohamed Yousef Khalil
abstract: Backfill materials play a critical role in governing heat-transfer efficiency, borehole thermal resistance, and the sizing of ground heat exchangers (GHEs), yet their selection is often treated as a secondary construction detail. Therefore, this paper presents a state-of-the-art review and comparative assessment of geothermal backfill materials, synthesizing experimental, numerical, and field-scale evidence. Conventional bentonite and cementitious grouts, quartz-rich sands, thermally enhanced grouts, controlled low-strength materials (CLSM), and phase-change-material (PCM) backfills are systematically evaluated. The reviewed studies indicate that conventional bentonite and cement-based grouts typically exhibit thermal conductivity values ranging from approximately 0.4 to 1.5 W/m·K, whereas quartz-rich sands and silica-enhanced materials generally range between 1.5 and 3.0 W/m·K. Thermally enhanced grouts, particularly graphite- and carbon-based mixtures, demonstrate the highest thermal conductivity values, often exceeding 3.0–4.0 W/m·K, with some studies reporting values approaching 5.0 W/m·K, significantly reducing borehole thermal resistance and improving heat transfer performance. The review further demonstrates that graphite-enhanced cementitious grouts achieve the highest thermal conductivity and lowest borehole thermal resistance, whereas optimized CLSM formulations offer balanced performance in terms of thermal efficiency, constructability, and sustainability. PCM-based backfills are shown to be particularly effective for thermal buffering under peak or cyclic operating conditions. In several reported cases, PCM-enhanced backfills improved thermal stability and reduced peak temperature fluctuations by approximately 15–30%, enhancing system performance under variable load conditions. Overall, the findings highlight that backfill selection should be treated as a primary design parameter in GHE systems, with material choice aligned to project-specific performance, cost, and long-term reliability objectives.

title: Reducing uncertainty in standing column well simulation through analytical inversion of deconvolved impulse responses
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Louis Jacques, Alain Nguyen, Philippe Pasquier, Gabriel Dion
abstract: Standing column wells achieve enhanced heat transfer through convergent groundwater flow, which is primarily stimulated by bleed operation. In the literature, thermal response tests applied to standing column wells have generally been interpreted using conventional conductive analytical models or detailed numerical models. Interpreting thermal response tests under such conditions is challenging because purely conductive models cannot capture advective effects, while numerical modeling requires substantial effort in model development, parameterization, and calibration. The analytical β -ILS model, recently introduced in the literature, addresses these challenges by accounting for advective heat transport in standing column wells operating with bleed. However, the β -ILS model has not yet been applied to interpret thermal response tests. This study presents a first interpretation methodology for the β -ILS model, which targets five key thermal and hydraulic properties and demonstrates that using impulse response functions improves estimation precision. Key thermal and hydraulic properties are estimated from thermal response test data using Bayesian inference to quantify parameter uncertainty. Two calibration strategies are compared: a conventional temperatures-based inversion and an alternative approach based on deconvolved impulse response functions derived from the same dataset. Results show that impulse-responses-based calibration improves the precision of inferred parameters. Notably, the uncertainty in effective heat exchange length decreases from 59% to 13%, while the mean absolute error on simulated temperatures improves from 0.38 ± 0.15 ° C (temperatures-based) to 0.32 ± 0.04 ° C (impulse-responses-based). These findings demonstrate that conducting impulse-response based interpretation with the β -ILS model enables more precise and computationally efficient property identification for standing column wells, supporting integration into design workflows for ground source heat pump systems.

title: Characterization of deep-seated geology and fracture system of the hot dry rock reservoir based on deep boreholes in the Gonghe Basin, northeastern Qinghai-Tibet plateau
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Linyou Zhang, Guilin Zhu, Xufeng Li, Zhaoxuan Niu, Shengsheng Zhang, Qingda Feng, Wenhao Xu, Zhihui Deng, Xianpeng Jin
abstract: The Gonghe Basin, located at the northeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, is endowed with abundant high geothermal resources. Several deep wells have been drilled within the Gonghe Basin to extract high-temperature fluids. In the framework of the hot dry rock resources exploration and production demonstration project, the recent drilling of the wells at 4 km depth, where the bottom hole temperature reaches about 209 °C, has enabled a clearer understanding of the deep-seated geology of the hot dry rock reservoir in the Gonghe Basin. In this paper, the deep-seated lithology, temperature distribution, and fracture characteristics of the hot dry rock reservoir with depth were analyzed based on observations of drill cores and cuttings, as well as well logging data. Furthermore, a conceptual model of both the deep geology and the fracture network of the hot dry rock reservoir was provided in the light of these recent investigation. The properties established in this report are expected to provide a basis for the rock property assumptions required in future models and simulations in the Gonghe Basin.

title: Magnetotelluric imaging of crustal structure beneath the Gulu geothermal system, Tibetan Plateau: Implication for REE enrichment
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Yue Shen, Yuanzhi Cheng, Yanlong Kong, Zhonghe Pang
abstract: The Gulu geothermal field, located in the northern Yadong–Gulu Rift, has the highest development potential in Tibet, as it contains concentrated geothermal reserves, and rare earth element (REE) resources. In this study, two nearly orthogonal broadband magnetotelluric sounding profiles were obtained at the northern end of the Gulu Rift zone. The impedance tensor method was used to qualitatively analyze the tectonic dimensions of the crustal structure in the study area. A reliable electrical structure of the crust was then obtained using the three-dimensional isotropic inversion method. The results indicate that the high-resistivity body observed in the upper crust below the Gulu geothermal system is consistent with Quaternary sediment, while the low-resistivity anomaly near the surface is consistent with the hydrothermal system. A number of low-resistivity anomalies were also observed at middle and lower crustal depths that were connected via low-resistivity channels to the near-surface low-resistivity regions. A comprehensive analysis was performed to determine the REE enrichment mechanism.
