During the ascent of mantle-derived hot material and magma generated by crustal re-melting, REEs such as Li, Rb, and Cs were continuously extracted from the surrounding rock. These REEs were transported into the upper crust, where they mixed with deep circulating groundwater from atmospheric precipitation and melting ice. This water was heated and geothermal water enriched in REEs was discharged to the surface.

title: Application of digital rock physics without segmentation to thermal conductivity estimation of Berea and Shirahama sandstones
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Yuhi Sakai, Kazuya Ishitsuka, Weiren Lin
abstract: Thermal conductivity is one of the most important physical properties of rocks and sediments for the industrial development of energy resources from geological formations, including geothermal energy extraction, enhanced oil recovery, and gas hydrate exploitation, as well as for understanding heat-related phenomena such as crustal heat flow and the subsurface temperature structure of active tectonic regions. Although conventional measurement techniques using probes and rock or sediment samples are well established, it is often impractical to measure all samples of interest because of limited sample availability or the large number of target specimens. In this study, to estimate the thermal conductivity of sandstone samples in a nondestructive, contactless, and efficient manner, this study developed a novel Digital Rock Physics (DRP) method that does not require segmentation of X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT) images. This method enables the use of XCT data with lower spatial resolution than existing DRP approaches by calculating intermediate physical properties for voxels representing multiple mineral or fluid phases. Raw XCT images were processed via continuous functions to convert CT values to density and subsequently to porosity; mixing laws were then applied to derive thermal conductivity, and arithmetic averaging was used to estimate specific heat capacity. Following numerical simulations of heat conduction, the DRP approach without segmentation was demonstrated to accurately estimate the effective thermal conductivity of two types of sandstones with different mineralogy and structures under dry and water-saturated conditions, in contrast to existing studies of thermal conductivity estimation. The proposed method enables the use of low-resolution XCT images for thermal conductivity estimation and significantly expands the availability of reliable thermal conductivity data efficiently and cost-effectively.

title: Thermal performance evaluation of geothermal energy pile using deep learning-based approaches – A comparative study
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Ashutosh Kumar, Ramakrishna Bag, Banavath Prasad Nayak, Divesh Ranjan Kumar
abstract: Geothermal energy piles (GEP) have been extensively studied in recent years due to their ability to combine structural support with geothermal energy harvesting, offering an energy-efficient and sustainable solution for heating and cooling applications. A comparative study of four deep learning algorithms was carried out to predict thermal conductance (Kc) and to analyse the thermal performance of geothermal energy piles. Sensitivity analysis and SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanation) analysis was also performed to identify key parameters affecting thermal performance. These include number of heat exchanger tubes (n), diameter of GEP (dp), inner diameter of heat exchanger tube (di), thickness of the heat exchanger tube (t), thermal conductivity of GEP (Kp), thermal conductivity of soil (Ks), thermal conductivity of heat exchanger tubes (Kt), and velocity of fluid (v). A dataset comprising 284 measurements of geothermal energy pile thermal conductance, incorporating eight influencing factors, was used to train and validate the proposed models. A thorough comparative evaluation of the models was performed to assess their effectiveness of models using various statistical indices, rank-based analysis, and an accuracy matrix. The effectiveness was further verified through internal model validation checks, while performance trends were illustrated using Taylor diagram. Among the evaluated models, RNN model demonstrated superior predictive performance, achieving highest coefficients of determination (R2 TR = 0.997, R2 TS = 0.991) and the lowest root mean square error (RMSETR = 0.833, RMSETS = 0.629). Sensitivity and SHAP analysis revealed that thermal conductivity of GEP is the most significant parameter in improving the thermal performance of the GEP, followed by other input parameters.

title: Enhancing Thermal energy storage in ground source heat pumps through phase change material integration: Experimental and numerical study
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Mehrdad Arastounia, Mohammad Hossein Jahangir
abstract: Ground source heat pump (GSHP) systems, while highly energy-efficient, often face long-term challenges such as soil thermal imbalance, outlet temperature fluctuations, and limited storage capacity. This study addresses these challenges by integrating phase change materials (PCMs) directly around borehole heat exchanger (BHE) tubes as thermal energy storage (TES). A laboratory-scale GSHP setup was developed, consisting of a cement-based BHE with a copper U-tube and circulating water loop. Two PCMs, phenol (melting point 40.5 °C) and phosphoric acid (melting point 21 °C), were selected for their suitability within the system’s operational temperature range. Experiments under high-temperature (45 °C) and low-temperature (5 °C) conditions, combined with numerical simulations, demonstrated that PCM-based TES improved outlet fluid temperature stability. Phenol in heating-dominant conditions improved outlet temperatures up to 3 °C, corresponding to a normalized temperature improvement (NTI) of 10.2 % compared to the baseline case. phosphoric acid reduced fluctuations by 0.5–1 °C with a relative temperature stabilization (RTS) of 2.1 % under cooling operation. Conductivity enhancement with 10 % vol. aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) further accelerated thermal charging/discharging, raising outlet temperatures by 3–4 °C during phase transitions without compromising latent heat storage. The addition of aluminum oxide increased the NTI in the high-temperature mode to 29.6 % and enhanced the RTS of the low-temperature mode to 4.1 %, demonstrating enhanced thermal performance due to increased conductivity. Simulation results corroborated experimental findings and revealed optimal design parameters for the PCM-based TES module. Overall, the results confirm that PCMs can effectively buffer thermal fluctuations and provide a scalable pathway for integrating advanced TES into GSHP systems.

title: Leveraging 3D seismic data and analogues to reduce uncertainty in the architecture and sedimentary infill of Permo-Carboniferous grabens: Implications for geothermal exploration
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Ovie Emmanuel Eruteya, Silvia Omodeo-Salé, Yasin Makhloufi, Andrea Moscariello
abstract: Permo-Carboniferous (PC) grabens in the Northern Alpine Foreland Basin represent key archives of post-Variscan tectonics and potential geo-energy systems. However, their geometry and infill remain poorly understood due to their burial depth and the limited availability of geophysical imaging and borehole control. Here, we present a structural and stratigraphic interpretation of the pre-Mesozoic succession from the 3D seismic reflection dataset from the St. Gallen area. This was integrated with a regional 2D seismic and borehole data from the Weiach-1 borehole penetrating the entirety of the Constance-Frick Trough as an analogue. Our results reveal a prominent horst-and-graben system dominantly oriented SSW-NNE within the Paleozoic basement, formed under extensional stresses associated with Late Paleozoic Variscan tectonics. We identify three principal structures—Unterlören Graben, St. Gallen Graben above the horst, and the Waldstatt-Herisau Graben—constrained by the seismic volume. These grabens exhibit complex fault geometries and heterogeneous internal facies. The facies exhibit high-amplitude, semi-parallel reflections interpreted as Carboniferous coal-bearing sometimes sandwiched within low-moderate amplitude facies overlain by lower-amplitude facies interpreted as Permian deposits. These findings suggest the presence of PC successions beneath St. Gallen in Switzerland. Furthermore, it suggests the structural framework may promote plumbing of deep-seated fluids to the shallower basin, with implications for geothermal energy development. Our study demonstrates the value of integrating seismic attribute analysis with well-calibrated analogues to reduce structural uncertainty and improve subsurface characterisation in tectonically complex, data-limited settings.

title: Experimental study on the influence of confining pressure on borehole bottom rock damage in pneumatic down-the-hole hammer drilling
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Pengyu Zhang, Jianming Peng, Yanliang Li, Yu Liu, Dong Ge, Baoyi Chen, Jiming Li, Boyu Shi, Zicheng Wang
abstract: With the development of deep geological resources, down-the-hole (DTH) hammer drilling technology has been increasingly adopted and promoted due to its high drilling efficiency. In this study, pneumatic DTH hammer drilling experiments on granite under different confining pressures were carried out using an autoclave. The results showed that as the confining pressure increased from 0 MPa to 18 MPa, the rate of penetration (ROP) decreased from 19.73 m/h to 8.05 m/h, representing a reduction of 59%. Dye-penetrant observation and crack distribution analysis of the borehole bottom rocks showed that although the damaged zone at the borehole bottom was significantly reduced under higher confining pressure, severe damage still existed in the vicinity of the drill bit. Furthermore, ultrasonic velocity tests, uniaxial compression tests, and Brazilian splitting tests were performed on the borehole bottom rock samples to analyze the extent of mechanical property degradation under different confining pressures. The DTH hammer remains effective in generating wellbore damage under confining pressure conditions. For example, the specimen suffered a compressive strength loss of 66.7% at 0 MPa confining pressure, and a loss of 17.2% at 18 MPa confining pressure, relative to the intact rock. This study provides insights into the borehole bottom rock fragmentation during DTH hammer drilling under confining pressure, revealing its unique capability of weakening formation rock strength to enhance drilling efficiency. The findings will help optimizing drilling parameters and bit teeth configuration under various formation conditions, improving bit service life.

title: Integrated geophysical insights into the structural controls on geothermal systems in the Tatun Volcano group, northern Taiwan
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): T. Lan-Chi Nguyen, Wen-Jeng Huang, Chien-Chih Chen, Chi-Shu Yen, Yi-Heng Li, Horng-Yuan Yen
abstract: Geothermal systems suitable for power generation require sufficient temperatures, favorable structural conditions, and reservoir permeability at depths shallower than ∼3–5 km. This study investigates geothermal resources and prospective development sites in the Tatun Volcano Group (TVG), northern Taiwan, using a new magnetotelluric/audio-magnetotelluric (MT/AMT) dataset integrated with gravity, magnetic, microseismic, borehole, and geological information. A 3D resistivity model was constructed from MT inversion, and seven geological cross-sections were developed using the kink method and refined with multiple geophysical constraints to relate resistivity structures to subsurface geology. Two geothermal systems are identified—the Mt. Qixing–Matsao–Mt. Shamao and Mt. Huangzui–Dayoukeng–Mt. Dajianhou systems—each characterized by a low-resistivity clay cap (<10 Ωm) overlying a moderately resistive reservoir (10–60 Ωm). A deep high-resistivity batholith and steep intrusive bodies spatially align with the Jin-shan and Shan-chiao faults. Both geothermal systems occur within hanging-wall domains, which also host dense microseismic clusters, whereas adjacent footwalls consist of either high-resistivity volcanic units or thick conductive altered zones, both indicative of low-permeability conditions that inhibit fluid flow. These relationships demonstrate that fault architecture governs the localization of fractured reservoirs and hydrothermal upflow pathways. We interpret the batholith as the principal magmatic heat source and the fault-controlled structural framework as the primary regulator of reservoir distribution. Together, these findings highlight the hanging-wall regions of the Jin-shan and Shan-chiao faults as priority targets for future geothermal exploration and development in the TVG.

title: Solar-assisted borehole thermal energy storage coupled with heat pump for livestock buildings: results from a full-scale installation
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Francesco Tinti, Carlos Alejandro Perez Garcia, Panteleimon Bakalis, Iván Acosta-Pazmiño, Stefano Benni
abstract: Livestock farming is an energy-intensive sector of agriculture and a significant contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. This study presents the first-year operational results of an integrated renewable energy system combining photovoltaic–thermal (PVT) collectors, borehole thermal energy storage (BTES), and a dual-source heat pump (DSHP) for space heating in a commercial swine nursery building. The BTES is based on a novel “double-circuit” configuration, allowing the exploitation of solar energy during mid-season and summer periods, while ensuring reliable heat supply during winter peak loads. A monitoring system, including dedicated piezometers aligned with groundwater flow, was implemented to continuously record environmental conditions inside the building, system operating parameters, energy flows, and subsurface temperature variations. During the first year, the system met the heating demand of the nursery barn, achieving an overall Seasonal Performance Factor (SPF) of 3.78. Approximately 54% of the heat pump operation occurred in hybrid ground–air mode, 38% in ground-only mode, and only 7% in air-only mode, demonstrating the effectiveness of the strategy in balancing performance and resource preservation. The installed system employed only 240 m of borehole heat exchangers, compared to an estimated 640 m required for conventional systems delivering comparable thermal performance. Subsurface monitoring confirmed that the thermal impact on the aquifer was limited and remained well below regulatory thresholds. The results demonstrate that solar-assisted BTES coupled with a DSHP represents a technically effective, energy-efficient, and environmentally compatible solution for decarbonising heating in livestock buildings, particularly in rural areas with available land and suitable hydrogeological conditions.

title: Mineral and geochemical evolution of granite under thermo-hydro-chemical (THC) coupled reactions with acidic geothermal water in the Qinghai-Tibet plateau
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Xin Liao, Jiuchen Long, Mingyao Zhong, Yu Tan, Wenda Zhang, Jiannan Chen, Yangshuang Wang, Ying Wang, Yunhui Zhang
abstract: The Qinghai–Tibet Plateau is characterized by intense tectonic activity, abundant geothermal resources, high geothermal gradients, and locally developed acidic geothermal waters, which pose significant challenges to deep-buried tunnel construction. Under such geothermal conditions, complicated thermo-hydro-chemical (THC) coupled interactions between granitic rocks and geothermal fluids may significantly affect rock integrity and engineering stability. This study obtained granite samples from an underground location at depths of 1000 to 1100 m in the Gonjo Basin of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China. The granite samples were submerged in solutions with various pH (3 to 7) and temperatures (60 to 120 °C) to mimic the pH and temperature of the local geothermal water. The geochemistry of the solutions and the mineral compositions, microstructures, and mechanical strength of the granite were investigated during or after the water-rock interaction under varying THC conditions. The results indicate that the lower pH promotes the dissolution of feldspar minerals, particularly anorthite. At 60 °C, the concentration of calcium (Ca) reaches 80 mg/L at pH = 3, and the concentration of potassium (K) shows a fluctuating trend, characterized by an initial rise, a decline, and a subsequent rebound at pH = 3 and 5. The high-temperature water-rock interactions under three temperature conditions predominantly occurred within the first 12 h. Elevated temperature exerted a more pronounced effect on the release of Na and Si, whereas its influence on Ca release exhibited an opposite trend. Notably, at 60 °C, the Ca concentrations were consistently higher (by approximately 30–50 mg/L) than those at 90° C at each stage. It appears that the dissolution of feldspar minerals has altered the microstructure of granite, resulting in rounded particle edges and surface microcracks. After the THC-coupled reaction, the elastic modulus and peak compressive strength of granite decreased by >13%. These results provide insight into the mineralogical and geochemical evolution of granite in geothermal environments and offer a scientific basis for the design and construction of deep tunnels in the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau and other geothermal regions worldwide.

title: Quantitative assessment of fluoride enrichment mechanisms and consequent health risks in geothermal waters of the Yishu Fault Zone using hydrochemical and multi-isotopic (H, O, Sr, S) tracers
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Luyao Wang, Kai Liu, Shouchuan Zhang, Li Wan, Fangyuan Jiang, Hui Feng, Yaoyao Zhang, Longqiang Zhang, Jialiang Wang
abstract: Sustainable exploitation of geothermal resources in the Yishu Fault Zone (YSFZ), a critical tectonic region in eastern China, is constrained by pronounced fluoride (F−) enrichment, posing a direct public health risk. To clarify the governing enrichment mechanisms and assess associated health risks, this study integrates hydrochemical data, multi-isotope tracers (H, O, Sr, S), and multivariate statistical analysis. The geothermal waters are identified as meteoric in origin, recharged from adjacent high-elevation mountainous areas, and their chemical composition evolves primarily through dissolution of evaporites (e.g., halite, gypsum) and carbonate minerals (e.g., calcite), along with significant cation exchange. These high-temperature Cl–Na type waters exhibit elevated F− concentrations (0.98–7.50 mg/L), with 90.9% exceeding the WHO drinking water guideline (1.5 mg/L). This enrichment is attributed to synergistic hydrogeochemical processes: (1) enhanced fluorite dissolution due to calcite and dolomite precipitation; (2) competitive adsorption–desorption under alkaline conditions (pH up to 9.57); and (3) cation exchange that reduces aqueous Ca2+ concentrations. Quantitative analysis shows that mineral dissolution–precipitation and competitive adsorption–desorption as the dominant controlling processes, accounting for 46.10% and 43.19% of the total fluoride enrichment, respectively. Health risk assessment reveals significant non-carcinogenic risks, particularly for infants (Total Hazard Quotient up to 11.73). This work not only quantifies the dominant controls on F− mobility in fault-controlled geothermal systems but also highlights the associated health risks, thereby providing a critical scientific basis for their safe and sustainable management.

title: Permeability evolution during long-term matrix acidification of sandstone under reservoir conditions
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 140 Author(s): Angel Ramirez, Leandra Weydt, Claire Bossennec, Tien Hung Pham, Gabriela Schubert, Stefanie Schmidt, Ingo Sass
abstract: Matrix acidification is widely applied to enhance near-wellbore transmissivity in reservoir rocks; however, its efficiency remains difficult to predict because long-term fluid–rock interactions under realistic reservoir conditions are not fully understood. The combined effects of chemical reactions and time-dependent deformation during prolonged acid injection remain insufficiently constrained. This study investigates permeability evolution in sandstone during prolonged injection of dilute hydrochloric acid (0.0375 wt% HCl; pH 2.0) under controlled temperature and stress conditions representative of geothermal reservoirs. Five flow-through experiments were conducted using a thermo-triaxial device, allowing coupled thermo–hydro–mechanical conditions to be maintained over extended durations. Permeability, axial and radial strain, and fluid chemistry were continuously monitored, while mineralogical changes and dissolved element concentrations were analyzed before, during, and after testing. After approximately 25 days of continuous flow, permeability increased in four of the five samples, although the magnitude and timing of the response varied between experiments. Permeability evolution cannot be explained by mineral dissolution alone but instead reflects the coupled influence of spatially localized fluid–rock reactions, thermally and chemically enhanced creep, and stress-controlled pore reorganization. These results demonstrate that long-term permeability evolution during geothermal acidification is governed by interacting thermo–hydro–mechanical–chemical (THMC) processes rather than purely geochemical effects, providing new constraints for reservoir stimulation strategies and reactive transport modelling approaches.

title: Characteristics of the present-day geothermal field and thermal structure of the lithosphere in the Huazhou-Huayin area, Weihe Basin
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Kai Qi, Xinlei Cai, Qianyi Li, Yang Zhang, Zhanli Ren, Zheng Li, Guoqiang Zhang, Mingpu Fan, Fenfei Bai, Zhuo Han, Lijun Zhu
abstract: Research on geothermal fields and lithospheric thermal structure is crucial for understanding regional tectonic dynamics and assessing geothermal resource potential. The Huazhou-Huayin area of the Weihe Basin exhibits significant geothermal anomalies, yet detailed studies on its present-day geothermal field and deep lithospheric thermal structure remain limited. Utilizing the latest drilling-logging data, borehole temperature measurements, rock thermophysical property tests, and geophysical data, this study systematically analyzes the characteristics and spatial variations of the present-day geothermal field. Combined with the heat conduction equation and geothermal parameters, this paper calculates the key features of the deep thermal structure, quantitatively assess the thermal state of the lithosphere, and discuss the controlling effects of deep-shallow factors on the geothermal field. This enables the establishment of a genetic model for the Huazhou-Huayin geothermal field. The results indicate that: 1) The geothermal gradient in the Huazhou-Huayin area decreases northward, averaging 33.3 °C/km but exceeding 36 °C/km in the southern piedmont zone. The average surface heat flow is 69.01 mW/m2, classifying the area as a medium-high temperature geothermal system. 2) The present-day Moho temperature ranges between 600 and 840 °C. Deep mantle heat flow (29–45 mW/m2) contributes 48–60% of the surface heat flow, reflecting a "cold crust-hot mantle" thermal structure. 3) The present-day thermal lithosphere thickness (TLT) varies from 70 to 120 km, thinning southward and thickening northward. The medium-high geothermal field is primarily controlled by deep mantle heat flow, crustal radiogenic heat (>32%), and fault structures, while basement relief and magmatic activity have relatively minor influence. The formation mechanism of geothermal field in the study area is attributed to the Cenozoic extensional stretching of the Weihe Basin, asthenospheric upwelling generating high mantle heat flow, continuous radiogenic heat production from the upper crust and Cenozoic, and enhanced hydrothermal convection facilitated by deep-seated major faults.

title: Electrical resistivity characterization of the freshwater-saline interface: Implications for groundwater heat pump deployment in carbonate islands
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Daniel Abraham González Orellana, Fernando Corbo-Camargo, Selene Olea Olea, Héctor Miguel Aviña Jiménez
abstract: Saline intrusion in coastal zones and islands must be carefully assessed and managed to avoid adverse environmental impacts on ecosystems and ensure the protection of freshwater resources for human consumption. This study employs electrical resistivity methods, specifically Vertical Electric Soundings, as the primary tool for characterizing aquifer salinity. Spatial variations in resistivity are analyzed and associating them with different salinity zones, allowing the delineation of the freshwater lens base. This information is essential for identifying aquifer conditions suitable for the deployment of Groundwater Heat Pump systems and for sustainable freshwater uses. Additionally, a preliminary comparative analysis between conventional Air Source and Groundwater Heat Pumps is presented, based on one year of experimental data. This comparative assessment provides an initial evaluation of the geothermal potential for the implementation of sustainable cooling systems in carbonate islands.

title: In-situ evaluation of undisturbed ground temperature for geothermal heat exchange applications in the National Capital Region, India
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Rajni Saggu
abstract: A precise determination of average annual ground temperature, also known as undisturbed ground temperature, is a key parameter in determining the heat exchange potential of the ground-coupled heat exchangers. This study evaluates in-situ undisturbed ground temperature by taking temperature measurements along 100 m in the ground. Temperature sensors were installed at every 10 m depth interval, and temperature measurements were taken at 10-min time intervals, over a period of one year (March 2024 to February 2025). To ascertain the air temperature influence zone, another set of investigations was performed by installing temperature sensors in the ground at 2 m depth intervals up to 10 m, then at 15 m, and at every 10 m depth from 20 m to 100 m. The findings indicate that the ground temperature variations depend on actual weather conditions and are affected by the diurnal cycle. Along the depth, temperature variations show significantly changed trends in different months of the year. Near-surface ground temperatures exhibit considerable fluctuations, following seasonal air temperature variations. Whereas the influence of prevailing air fluctuations progressively diminishes at lower depths, offering a nearly steady temperature over the year. The existence of stable soil temperatures in deeper layers indicates that horizontal ground heat exchangers would not function efficiently in the region under consideration; therefore, vertical ground-coupled heat exchangers would be the preferred option. Time-dependent thermal response of near-surface ground highlights complex ground-atmosphere interactions, and depth-dependent temperature variations suggest that the weather-affected ground conditions impact the assessment of undisturbed ground temperature. Therefore, an understanding of temporal and depth-wise variations in ground temperature throughout the seasons of the year is essential for determining the use of ground-coupled heat exchangers.

title: Integrating geological, engineering, and economic indexes in geothermal play fairway mapping: A case study from the Vienna pull-apart basin
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Lucia Ledvényiová, Michal Nemčok, Samuel Rybár
abstract: This study develops a GIS-based, categorical geothermal play fairway map for a pull-apart basin and applies it to the Czech sector of the Vienna Basin. It is intended as a quick, easily reproducible basic evaluation of the geothermal potential in pull-apart basins, based on pre-existing data from hydrocarbon exploration in known petroleum province. Six geological, engineering, and economic indexes (e.g. thermoelectric production index, potential for scaling and corrosion, investment return potential) were calculated from data available from the petroleum industry to evaluate electric power-generation potential. Although fluid flow rates are locally favorable, geothermal fluid temperatures are too low for Organic Rankine Cycle operation, resulting in uniformly poor outlet-temperature and cost indexes. The integrated play fairway map, therefore, indicates no viable potential for the power generation. However, temperature and flow-rate patterns suggest that parts of the basin may be suitable for the direct-use geothermal heating.

title: Operational optimization of deep borehole heat exchangers: Numerical evidence on cross-seasonal heat storage mitigating ground cold accumulation
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Jiachen Wang, Chao Li, Chao Jiang, Liguo Zhao, Jiale Wu, Yun Wang
abstract: To mitigate ground cold accumulation during heat transfer in deep borehole heat exchangers (DBHEs), this study proposes a cross-seasonal heating and cooling supply (CCHS) strategy. The proposed strategy extracts heat over the full depth of the borehole during the heating season. It utilizes shallow ground thermal storage during the transitional period, thereby reducing cold accumulation at specific depths. Using quasi-three-dimensional full-scale simulations based on ANSYS Fluent, the study compares heat extraction, natural recovery, and thermal storage across four scenarios: conventional DBHEs, variations in bore diameter depths (or depths of thermal storage), thermal storage water temperatures, and the presence or absence of thermal storage. The results show that, despite a prolonged natural recovery period, heat extraction performance declines gradually over time. The presented CCHS strategy effectively mitigates heat transfer degradation, with performance efficiency closely linked to thermal storage water temperature and depth. Specifically, when the depth is 400 m and the thermal storage water temperature is 63°C, the CCHS approach improves heat transfer by 1.54% and reduces the degradation rate by 2.08% in the fifth year. This research offers valuable theoretical and technical insights for developing medium- and deep-geothermal systems, enhancing the long-term stability and efficiency of DBHEs.

title: Geological structures and thermal regime along volcanoes and basement rocks of Tangyin rift geothermal field from resistivity survey and Radon detection
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Jianhua Ping, Joshua Mahwa, Wei Leng, Jichang Zhao, Jiaqi Liu
abstract: Geothermal resource assessment requires a clear understanding of the subsurface thermal regime and geological framework. The Tangyin rift area, located in eastern Taihang Mountains, China, presents a promising geothermal prospect due to magmatic intrusions within carbonate and sandstone formations, which can heat deep groundwater. However, exploration at depth remains challenging due to cost and logistical constraints. This study employs audio-frequency magnetotelluric (AMT) surveys and radon gas measurements to characterize the geothermal system. Results reveal consistent resistivity and radon anomalies with a Pearson correlation coefficient of r = −0.083, delineating a cap layer, a potential carbonate reservoir, radiogenic heat sources, and fault-controlled fluid pathways. The Hebi volcano and associated granitoid intrusions act as primary heat sources, while fractured carbonate and sandstone units form the reservoir. Faults and unconformities facilitate fluid circulation. Although the cap layer may limit shallow exploitation, the estimated reservoir temperature (120–220 °C) and reservoir depth (1700 m) indicate moderate geothermal potential suitable for direct-use applications, contributing to local sustainable energy strategies. This integrated approach demonstrates the effectiveness of combining AMT and radon surveys for cost-effective geothermal exploration in complex geological settings.

title: Radiogenic heat production of the East Volga region: A systematic study
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Igor Ognev, Valentin Kuzin, Pavel Kotler, Anna Kulikova, Rafael Muzafarov
abstract: Radiogenic heat production (RHP) is a critical parameter controlling lithospheric temperatures and surface heat flow in stable continental regions, yet is poorly constrained in cratonic terranes overlain by sedimentary cover. We present the first systematic study of RHP in the eastern part of the Volgo–Uralian segment of the East European Craton based on gamma-ray spectrometric measurements from 143 boreholes penetrating the crystalline basement. RHP exhibits substantial lateral heterogeneity, ranging from 0.01 to 14.3 μW/m³ with a mean of 2.0 μW/m³, approximately three times higher than typical Archean cratons. Vertical profiling along a 3.1 km basement section in the Minnibaevo 20,000 well reveals that RHP variations are controlled by rock type rather than depth, with elevated values in high-alumina metasedimentary rocks and low values in metabasic rocks. Bayesian inversion with a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach, constrained by surface heat flow and lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary temperature, yields estimates of sedimentary and lower crustal heat production distributions as well as thickness variation of the enriched upper crustal layer. The East Volga region exhibits a high degree of crustal differentiation with an average differentiation index of 2.3. Notably, upper crustal RHP shows a moderate negative correlation with surface heat flow, indicating that the classical heat flow province concept does not apply in the East Volga region. X-Ray fluorescence analysis identifies potassium content as the primary control on RHP in igneous and metaigneous rocks, and alumina content in metasedimentary rocks.

title: Organic matter in thermal springs, the Central part of the Baikal Rift Zone
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): V.A. Poturay, E.V. Zippa, A.V. Ukraintsev, I.A. Fedorov, A.S. Toropov
abstract: A variety of organic compounds in the thermal waters of the Central Baikal Rift Zone were studied. The research was based on solid-phase extraction method that was carried out in-situ. We considered N2-thermal waters of SO4-Natype and N2-CH4 thermal waters of HCO3-SO4-Na type with temperatures at the surface ranging between 19.8–75.6 °C. We identified 211 organic components with molecular weights from 92 to 506 daltons using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. The dissolved organic carbon concentration was on average 0.7 mg/L. DOC origin is autochthonous with a small contribution from plant detritus. It was established that normal and iso-alkanes, aromatic hydrocarbons and ethers are dominant organic compounds in the thermal springs. The origin of these compounds is predominantly bacterial with the contribution of thermocatalytic processes in the formation of some linear alkanes and aromatic hydrocarbons. In addition, we found correlation between the main homologous series of organic matter, major ions and physicochemical parameters. These correlations showed a decrease of ethers and phthalates concentrations and an increase of heteroaromatic hydrocarbons and terpenes content due to an increase of fluorine ion. Moreover, the terpenes accumulation impacts DOC which concentration increases too. In turn, aliphatic hydrocarbons initiate the formation of aromatic ones, entering reactions of cycloaddition, polymerization, dehydrocyclization, etc. In addition, some compounds indicate an insignificant technogenic pollution of the studied thermal springs in the Central Baikal Rift Zone.

title: Reflection seismic surveying at the volcanic geothermal system of Petra (Lesvos Island, Greece)
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Emmanouil Konstantinidis, George Apostolopoulos, Alireza Malehmir, Myrto Papadopoulou, Magdalena Markovic, Ioannis Vakalas, Haralabos Kranis, Emmanouil Skourtsos
abstract: The Petra morphological depression on Lesvos Island hosts one of Greece’s most promising low- to intermediate-enthalpy geothermal prospects, yet its internal structure and fluid pathways remain poorly constrained. To improve the characterization of the geothermal system, an integrated geophysical survey combining seismic, gravity, and magnetic methods was conducted in 2024 to delineate basin geometry and identify fault and fracture zones with enhanced permeability. Reflection seismic data were processed to image subsurface structure, while point-diffraction modelling was applied to constrain migration velocities and distinguish structural discontinuities from faults and small-scale intrusive bodies. First-break traveltime tomography provided complementary constraints on fault geometry and on the thickness of fresh volcanic units (Upper Lava), and residual gravity data were used to resolve lateral density variations. The integrated interpretation reveals a fault-bounded depression filled with low-density, low-velocity Upper Lava overlying higher-velocity, higher-density Lower Lava. Two major sets of steeply dipping faults define the Petra depression; minor and intersected faults are considered as conduits that enhance permeability and promote hydrothermal circulation. The Petra depression is interpreted as a small transtensional pull-apart basin that localizes geothermal fluid flow along its major fault zones. From a geothermal perspective, these results reduce structural uncertainty and highlight two domains along the northern and southern bounding faults as the most promising targets for future geothermal drilling.

title: A study of geothermal energy sweep efficiency improvement in the Williston Basin based on oil/gas engineering concepts
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Dongmei Wang, Yun Ji, William Gosnold, Olufemi Oni
abstract: This paper presents a new study of geothermal energy based on oil/gas engineering concepts. Remediation of channeling in geothermal applications is examined using biopolymer gel. The effectiveness of this gel is considered through rock fracture analysis, bottom-hole-temperature correlation, laboratory experiments and subsurface modeling, along with analysis of the economic feasibility for field application. Generally, micro fractures aid heat extraction through fracture networks. However, once severe channeling develops, the efficiency of heat extraction will decrease. To prevent the hot fluids from channeling through large apertures, a biopolymer gel agent was developed at the University of North Dakota. The specific objective is for the biopolymer agent to reduce channeling through the most conductive fractures while diverting aqueous fluids through less-conductive fracture pathways. Major experiences we learned from a case study on a Deadwood Formation geothermal system include at a specified pressure gradient, for a gel treatment, there is no significant heat loss when the fluid reaches the production end compared to using only cold-water injections. Only a small gel slug size is needed to divert hot water to flow efficiently through the studied volume, with an enhanced hot water recovery of about 20%. This efficiency increase can generate sufficient revenue to cover the costs of the gel treatment.

title: Semi-analytical approach to the coupled plastic-softening THM response of a circular opening
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Aref Farahi, Hossein Salarirad, Ali Mortazavi
abstract: A semi-analytical solution is presented for the coupled strain-softening Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical (THM) response of a wellbore in a low-permeability reservoir during non-isothermal injection/production. An exponential function relates cohesion degradation to irreversible plastic strain. Seepage and thermally-induced stresses are treated as body forces in a plastic zone discretized into concentric annuli with perfect plasticity and a constant friction angle. Results reveal that tangential and radial stress distributions in the plastic zone are governed by the interplay between temperature, pore pressure, and strength softening. During hot injection, raising the temperature differential from 0°C to 40°C increases the ratio of Thermo-Hydro-Perfect-Plastic (THPP) to Thermo-Hydro-Softening-Plastic (THSP) tangential stress at the wellbore wall from 1.2 to 1.7. In contrast, with cold injection, this ratio drops from 1.2 to 1.0 when the temperature differential shifts from 0°C to -30°C. Compared to the initial cohesion, the rock mass cohesion at the wellbore wall declines by 54% during production and 68% during injection at a temperature differential of 40°C. At -40°C, the reductions are 29% and 26%, respectively. The results of this study reveal the significant effect of the plastic-softening THM coupling on the wellbore stress field. Ignoring this effect leads to conservative estimates of cohesion strength and tangential stress at wellbore, which can influence predictions of sand production potential and guide decisions about injection and production scenarios inside the reservoir.

title: Aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) for district heating and cooling systems: A review
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Mohammed B. Rabani, Alessandro Maccarini, Kathrin Menberg, Philipp Blum, Alireza Afshari
abstract: Seasonal thermal energy storage plays a pivotal role in transitioning district heating and cooling (DHC) systems toward the use of renewable energy. Among the available technologies, aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) emerges as a promising form of sensible heat storage, utilizing the subsurface as the storage medium. This study reviews the integration of ATES systems with DHC networks, drawing insights from various case studies in the literature. It identifies and summarizes real-world ATES implementations at district scale and explores different modeling approaches for coupling ATES with DHC systems. Furthermore, we identify technological, policy, and deployment challenges that hinder the current widespread adoption of ATES with district energy networks such as ATES oversizing during design phase, market uptake during implementation and thermal imbalances during operational phase. By synthesizing findings from multiple case studies, this review highlights the current state of ATES technology and its significant potential to enhance the flexibility, efficiency, and sustainability of modern low-carbon DHC systems. Furthermore, we also identify that using a holistic system approach in analysis can support decision makers in implementing ATES at a district scale.

title: Optimization reinjection strategies in a sandstone geothermal reservoir: Insights from laboratory experiments
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Jieqin Xia, Sadiq J. Zarrouk, Eylem Kaya, Hong Tian, Yanting Zhao, Jun Zheng, Bin Dou
abstract: Geothermal reinjection wells often suffer from limited injectivity and reservoir blockage, hindering continuous and efficient reinjection. Among the various factors influencing reinjection performance, four key engineering parameters, injection fluid flow rate, injection fluid temperature, perforation orientation, and operational mode, are both highly controllable and critical for optimization. This study investigates the near-wellbore reinjection behavior of sandstone from the Guantao Formation using experiments, exploring the dynamic permeability response under varying injection-fluid parameters and operational modes. Results show that reservoir injectivity is relatively insensitive to changes in flow rate but highly sensitive to confining pressure, which induces irreversible damage. The optimal injection flow rate at the field scale was determined to be 90 m3/h. Addressing the long-standing debate on injection fluid temperature, the experiments confirm that reducing the temperature difference between the injected fluid and the reservoir effectively mitigates irreversible thermal stress-induced damage, promoting long-term reservoir sustainability. Moreover, the optimal perforation azimuth was determined as 262°, corresponding to a 60° angle between the reservoir’s paleocurrent flow direction and the wellbore radial direction. Step-rate injection was proven to be the most effective operational mode for enhancing injectivity. Based on these findings, a practical reinjection strategy optimization framework is proposed, offering scientific guidance for efficient and sustainable reinjection of sandstone geothermal reservoirs.

title: Opportunities for geothermal direct use in Mesillas geothermal prospect, Mexico
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): H.M. Aviña-Jiménez, R.M. Prol-Ledesma, M.A. García-Ávila, A.A. Rodríguez-Díaz, M.P. Jácome-Paz, D. Pérez-Zárate, I.A. González-Romo, J.L. Salas-Corrales
abstract: The Mesillas area is the westernmost geothermal prospect in the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt geothermal province, and in this work, it is characterized and evaluated for direct use. This prospect extends the favorable zone in this geothermal province towards the west coast of Mexico. The hydrothermal system is hosted in andesitic units that occur in an area of ∼1.5 km2, 25 thermal springs with discharge temperatures between 47–90 °C, and a pH ∼ 9. Intense CO2 and H2S degassing is observed in the highest temperature springs. The surface activity is related to intense fracturing associated with NW-SE, SW-NE, NS, and EW normal fault systems. Hydrothermal manifestations cluster in the reduced area where a Time-Domain Electromagnetic (TDEM) survey revealed very low resistivity anomalies that extend down to 400 m depth and outspread further south, suggesting the potentially large feasibility for the direct use of the geothermal resource. The success of geothermal exploitation in low and medium temperature systems is related to the development of direct use projects that are technically and socially viable. Therefore, this paper presents the characterization of Mesillas geothermal prospect with the results of advanced exploration and propose relevant direct uses of the resource. The presented results support the sustainability of this system’s exploitation and an efficient path to move from exploration to exploitation of geothermal energy resources.

title: Lightweight prototype-fusion YOLACT++ for multi-scale fracture identification in Gonghe Basin hot-dry-rock reservoirs
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Xiushi Jiang, Ben Dong, Haiwen Chen, Yuan Liang, Peng Zhao, Rongcai Song
abstract: Fracture systems play a critical role in controlling permeability structure and fluid circulation in hot dry rock (HDR) geothermal reservoirs, particularly in crystalline basement settings. In practice, fracture information is commonly derived from heterogeneous observational sources spanning multiple scales, including scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images, core photographs, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)–based surface images. However, fracture representations across these scales are often fragmented and difficult to integrate, which limits consistent geological interpretation and reservoir-scale characterization. To address this challenge, this study focuses on the automated extraction of fracture information across multiple observational scales, with the aim of improving the consistency and comparability of fracture descriptions in HDR reservoirs. A lightweight prototype-fusion YOLACT++ framework is developed to identify fracture patterns from SEM images, core images, and UAV images in the Gonghe Basin. The proposed framework integrates multi-scale feature representations while maintaining computational efficiency during the inference stage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves robust fracture identification performance across different image scales, preserving key geometric characteristics such as fracture continuity, orientation, and trace morphology. The lightweight design reduces computational cost while retaining competitive segmentation accuracy compared with baseline models. The extracted fracture information provides a coherent basis for subsequent geological interpretation and may serve as supporting input for fracture connectivity analysis and reservoir conceptual modeling in HDR systems.

title: Thermal performance testing of shallow geothermal systems: Insights from field experiments and numerical modelling
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Christopher S. Brown, Isa Kolo, Gioia Falcone, Daniel Friedrich, Sean M. Watson
abstract: Decarbonisation of the heating and cooling sectors is essential for achieving net zero targets, and geothermal systems provide a promising pathway to reduce reliance on fossil fuels. To design and optimise ground source heat pump (GSHP) systems, an understanding of subsurface thermal properties is critical. Traditionally, this is achieved through thermal response tests (TRTs), which measure subsurface behaviour under constant heat flux conditions. However, thermal performance tests (TPTs) offer an alternative approach by applying a constant inlet temperature, allowing not only the determination of effective thermal conductivity but also an assessment of the system’s thermal capacity under both heating and cooling scenarios. This study presents what is believed to be the UK’s first documented TPT and a new direct comparison of heat injection and extraction tests, aiming to demonstrate the method’s value for characterising geothermal systems in real-world applications. The experiments at the Cheshire Geoenergy Observatory consisted of two borehole heat exchangers (BHEs) injecting heat at a constant temperature of 30 °C and two BHEs extracting heat by circulating fluid at a set point of 1 °C within the Sherwood Sandstone Group. Results indicate that TPTs provided effective thermal conductivity estimates (2.43–3.65 W/mK) consistent with core measurements and numerical models. However, there are issues with heat extraction TPTs, which appear to under-estimate thermal conductivity. This could be due to (i) natural convection enhancing heat transfer in the subsurface during heat injection mode, or (ii) the oscillatory behaviours of heaters and chillers may introduce errors when estimating properties, potentially impacting this conclusion.

title: Mechanical and acoustic emission characteristics of sandstone after high-temperature and water-cooling treatment under true triaxial cyclic loading
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Kaihui Li, Rushan Yang, Qinghe Li, Dongya Han, Jie Yang, Mengxiang Wang
abstract: Understanding the thermo-mechanical response of reservoir rocks is critical for geothermal energy extraction; here, a series of true triaxial tests were performed on sandstone after high-temperature and water-cooling treatment to investigate its mechanical and acoustic emission (AE) behaviors under thermal-mechanical coupled true triaxial conditions, simulating the thermal shock experienced by reservoir rock during cold fluid injection in geothermal operations. The results demonstrate that the heat-treated temperature and intermediate principal stress (σ 2) significantly affect the mechanical properties and failure mechanism of sandstone. High temperature induces mineral phase transformations and microstructural reorganization in sandstone, markedly reducing its bearing capacity and promoting its plastic deformation, while increased σ 2 effectively suppresses the thermal damage. As the heat-treated temperature increases, the failure mode of sandstone specimen transitions from shear-dominated to tensile-dominated, with cyclic stress perturbations inhibiting the coalescence of thermal-induced tensile cracks. The AE results further reveal that the stage-specific characteristics of damage evolution in sandstone are closely related to the thermo-mechanical coupling effect and the critical slowing-down characteristics can serve as precursors to macroscopic failure. Additionally, it is found that the proportion of dissipated energy in specimen increases significantly under high-temperature conditions, reflecting a thermal damage-dominated plastic deformation mechanism. Whereas the high σ 2 enhances the elastic energy storage capacity of specimen, demonstrating the inhibitory effect of stress constraints on the rock damage development.

title: An analytical approach to production logging in enhanced geothermal systems using distributed fiber optic thermal slug tracking
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Rion Nakamoto, Smith Leggett
abstract: Short circuit pathways in an enhanced geothermal system (EGS) lead to early thermal breakthrough and subeconomic performance. Geothermal operators use production and injection logs to quantify the flow distribution across completion intervals to identify these pathways. One method for production logging in geothermal wells involves using distributed fiber optic sensing (DFOS) to correlate thermal slug velocities with bulk fluid velocities. A thermal slug is a thermal transient that moves along the wellbore via convection with the wellbore fluid. DFOS tracks the movement, or velocity, of thermal transients through the wellbore. In conventional practice, thermal slug velocities are often estimated arbitrarily by manually drawing lines along thermal signals in depth-time waterfall plots; this study establishes a more objective method to determine these velocities compared to subjective straight-line fitting by hand. Meanwhile, coupled wellbore-fracture-reservoir models can rigorously calculate bulk fluid velocities but are computationally demanding and analytically intractable. We hypothesize that flow distribution can be reasonably estimated based on convection and instantaneous conduction to highly conductive wellbore components. A sensitivity analysis was performed to investigate how key parameters affect thermal slug velocities. Findings showed that heat conduction to the surroundings resulted in slower such velocities; however, these velocities remained relatively unchanged even when the imposed inflow temperature was substantially altered or the thermal conductivity of relatively non-conductive surrounding rock doubled. The methods were further validated using data from a circulation test conducted on the Utah FORGE EGS, exhibiting strong consistency with field-inferred flow rates. This novel approach provides a reliable, efficient tool for improving flow diagnostics in EGS development.

title: Reactive transport modelling of CO 2 -enriched condensate reinjection in andesitic geothermal reservoirs towards the enhancement of carbon mineralisation
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Yeftamikha Siahaan, Eylem Kaya, Sadiq J. Zarrouk, Bridget Lynne
abstract: This study applies reactive transport modelling to investigate the geochemical and hydrodynamic impacts of CO2-enriched condensate reinjection into andesitic geothermal reservoirs, building on a high-temperature flow-through experiment using steam condensate and Southern Negros andesite at 230 °C and 200 bar. The calibrated model of the experiment resulted in significant quartz dissolution and secondary minerals deposition, with the magnitude of the dissolution being higher than the deposition, resulting in an increase in permeability. This calibrated model served as the basis for our fluid-rock interactions simulations under evolving CO2 conditions and additional chemicals. The model explores how increasing CO2 concentrations in the injected fluid influence fluid pH, mineral dissolution and precipitation trend, and permeability. We found that (i) a certain amount of CO2 could enhance calcite dissolution but promote anhydrite precipitation, (ii) increasing the CO2 mineralisation by adding Ca(OH)2 initiated mineralisation in the form of calcite, and (iii) the highest mineralisation was achieved by injecting the same moles of Ca(OH)2 with the injected CO2 and SO4 2-. This experimental-modelling approach enhances our understanding of reactive surface area evolution, CO2 storage mechanisms, and their effect on the reservoir performance in geothermal systems.

title: Long-lived brittle reactivation of crossing fault networks enhancing upwellings in hydrothermal systems: The case study of Chaudes-Aigues spring swarm
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Emmy Penhoët, Laurent Arbaret, Angélie Portal, Charles Gumiaux, Maxime Picault, Albane Canva, Béatrice Ledésert, Nicolas Maubec, Séverine Caritg, Laurent Guillou-Frottier
abstract: Identifying the structures that allow hydrothermal fluids to rise from a deep reservoir to surface thermal springs is a major geothermal challenge. Faults play an ambivalent role in this process: they can be effective drains or, on the contrary, impermeable barriers, depending on their geometry and their reactivation over geological time. The locations of thermal springs are directly linked to these structures, their architecture and particularly in fault zones intersections. Exploring this variability is essential to constrain the circulation mechanisms in geothermal systems. The Chaudes-Aigues hydrothermal system, French Massif Central, is a particularly suitable natural laboratory for exploring the relationship between faults and fluid flow. It is characterised by more than 30 thermal springs, some of the hottest in Europe (up to 82°C for the Par Spring), located at the intersection of three Variscan fault zones: N150E, N050E and N00E. These intersections create networks of concentrated fractures, likely to act as preferential conduits for fluid flow. Despite these structural indications, the precise upwelling drains remain poorly identified. This study, aimed at identifying these drains, combines field structural analysis, fault density mapping, lineament analysis and gravity inversion modeling. Fault density mapping reveals a clear contrast across the study area. The southwestern Margeride Granitic Complex (MGC) shows sparse faulting, while its northeastern extent exhibits high fault density in N150E-oriented corridors, particularly near Chaudes-Aigues and La Chaldette. Outcrop-scale fault zone analysis reveals three major types. One of them, made of thick ductile-to-brittle N050E trending shear zones, assumed to be highly permeable, would be the main upwelling drains of the system. Gravity modeling reveals that the MGC would be located at shallow depth beneath the thermal springs. Altogether, results demonstrate that inherited ductile fabrics, reactivated fault systems, and fracture connectivity exert first-order control on granite emplacement and hydrothermal flow. These findings refine the structural model of the Chaudes-Aigues system and highlight the critical role of tectonics in geothermal fluid circulation. This hydrothermal system illustrates how inherited structures may act either as impermeable barriers or efficient drains, once reactivated, a duality that controls the location and persistence of thermal springs.

title: Thermal waters of the Western Bohemian Massif (Germany): geothermometry, origin and circulation
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Simon Prause, Horst Kämpf, Gerhard Strauch, Alena Sophie Broge, Ferdinand Perssen, Jessica Alexandra Stammeier, Sascha Görne
abstract: The fault-bound basement-hosted geothermal systems of the Western Bohemian Massif (Germany) remain poorly constrained in terms of reservoir temperatures, circulation depths and recharge. Here, we present some of the first systematic constraints on these parameters based on a geochemical survey of regional thermal water, non-thermal groundwater and surface water, combining isotope techniques, a multi-method geothermometric approach and mixing calculations. Stable isotope ratios (δ18O and δ2H) indicate that all studied thermal waters are derived from meteoric precipitation. The geothermal reservoirs of the region are identified as low-enthalpy “hot water type” systems with temperatures generally < 100 °C. The occurrence of local warm springs is linked to radiogenic heating in primarily granitic reservoirs at depth and migration of thermal water to the surface along long-lived permeable fault systems. Despite having interacted with similar reservoir lithologies at comparable temperatures, thermal waters exhibit pronounced hydrochemical variability in terms of composition, mineralization and extent of water-rock interaction. These differences primarily reflect structural characteristics of the individual geothermal systems, such as hydraulic openness and fault connectivity, which in turn affect recharge rates, residence times, extent of dilution with non-thermal groundwater and the supply of dissolved CO2. Together, these results demonstrate that hydraulic connectivity and permeable fault architecture exert a first-order control on geochemical signatures in the geothermal systems of the Western Bohemian Massif and similar basement-hosted settings.

title: Carbon dioxide degassing and recharge processes in geothermal springs of the Kumaun Himalaya: Evidence from geochemical and isotopic data
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Sehajnoor Kaur, Sameer K. Tiwari, Ayushi Baiswar
abstract: Geothermal springs in active collisional orogens represent important natural pathways for crustal carbon transfer, yet their fluid evolution and degassing behavior remain insufficiently constrained in the Central Himalayas. This study integrates hydrochemical, stable isotopic, and dissolved and direct gaseous flux measurements to characterize geothermal systems in the Kumaun region. The waters are dominated by Ca-Mg-HCO₃ facies, indicating carbonate weathering and meteoric recharge along shallow, fault-controlled pathways, with rock-weathering control and limited deep volatile input. Stable δ¹⁸O-δD compositions cluster near the Global and Local Meteoric Water Lines, with minor ¹⁸O enrichment reflecting hydrothermal equilibration and longer subsurface residence relative to adjacent river waters. Carbon isotopes of dissolved inorganic carbon (δ¹³CDIC ≈ +5 to +8 ‰) indicate that carbonate dissolution and metamorphic decarbonation represent the dominant carbon sources, accompanied by substantial secondary carbonate precipitation during ascent. Integrated dissolved and direct flux measurements reveal that free-gas discharge is a significant and previously underestimated component of crustal degassing, with combined CO₂ emissions on the order of 10⁶ mol a⁻¹. Elevated ambient CO₂ and CH₄ concentrations confirm persistent, spatially distributed emissions. These results identify the Kumaun geothermal province as an active crustal CO₂ emission node within the Himalayan orogen and underscore its importance for mountain-belt carbon cycling and long-term atmospheric carbon regulation.

title: Geothermal prospect evaluation of northern Benue tough, northeastern Nigeria, from high resolution airborne magnetic data
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Olawale Olakunle Osinowo, Yusuf Abdulmumin, Tolulope Florence Lamidi
abstract: The Northern Benue Trough in northeastern Nigeria exhibits considerable potential for geothermal energy research, particularly owing to the existence of geothermal surface manifestations and its proximity to the Cameroon Volcanic Line. This study assesses the geothermal potential of the region using high-resolution airborne magnetic data obtained from the Nigeria Geological Survey Agency (NGSA). The Total Magnetic Intensity data from the study area were reduced to the equator to focus the anomalies directly on top of their sources, prior to further processing. Subsequently, lineament extraction was conducted using CET Grid analysis to identify structural elements that could influence geothermal systems. Spectral analysis was performed using the centroid approach across 76 overlapping blocks, each measuring 55 by 55 km with a 50 % overlap. Parameters obtained from the spectrum analysis were utilised to determine the Curie depth, geothermal gradient, and heat flow throughout the study area. The research delineates a prevailing NE-SW lineament trend, featuring structures that extend from 7 km to more than 170 km in length. Curie depths range from 18 to 46 km, while geothermal gradient and heat flow values span from 13 to 40°C/km and 54 to 94 mW/m², respectively. The western and northwestern regions, as well as the central and southeastern areas of the study site, predominantly exhibit elevated geothermal gradients (20-40°C/km) and increased heat-flow zones trending NW-SE. In contrast, the southern and eastern regions are characterised by lower values. The association of shallow Curie depths, high geothermal gradients, and regional lineaments suggests the possibility of geothermal development in areas with elevated geothermal gradients and heat flow. The findings highlight the opportunity to conduct systematic exploration to identify appropriate geothermal energy development opportunities, particularly in regions with high thermal activity.

title: Lithospheric extension and deep thermal evolution of the Northern South China sea continental slope: A case study of the Lingshui Sag, Qiongdongnan Basin
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Wei Wang, Yajun Li, Dujie Hou, Qian Cao, Weihe Chen, Xianzhuo Luo
abstract: The exploration community increasingly recognizes that the thermal regime of sedimentary basins fundamentally controls hydrocarbon generation and accumulation. As the most prolific domain for global hydrocarbon discoveries, passive continental margins have become a focal area for research on paleogeothermal field reconstruction. The Lingshui Sag (LSS) of the Qiongdongnan Basin (QDNB), located in the deepwater northern margin of the South China Sea (SCS), lacks constraints on its tectono-thermal evolution owing to limited drilling and geophysical data. Herein, on the basis of a noninstantaneous, multiphase uniform stretching model, we select four industrial and 45 pseudo-wells in the LSS using the strain rate method applied for inverting stretching factors and heat flow values, thereby continuously characterizing the features of lithospheric stretching and its thermal response across the ocean–continent transition zone. The tectono-thermal evolution of the LSS can be divided into three stages: (1) a rifting stage (33.9–23 Ma), which is characterized by rapid lithospheric thinning and a marked increase in heat flow, (2) a thermal subsidence stage (23–10.5 Ma), which is dominated by lithospheric cooling and a gradual decline in heat flow, and (3) a rapid subsidence stage (10.5 Ma–present), which is marked by enhanced tectonic subsidence and a rapid rebound in heat flow. The post-10.5 Ma heat flow rebound implies renewed post-rift tectonic activity in the ocean–continent transition zone, which may have promoted basin-scale reheating by modifying deep heat transfer pathways in this magma-poor margin. Sensitivity tests show that the temporal trends of stretching factor and heat flow remain stable across parameter scenarios, while radiogenic heat production and paleowater depth correction primarily govern the magnitude of modeled heat flow. QDNB represents a typical warm margin when compared with global passive margins. During rifting, its thermal state is mainly controlled by lithospheric thinning and mantle upwelling, with mantle-derived heat flow playing a dominant role. By contrast, post-rift regional tectonic events are crucial for interrupting lithospheric cooling and triggering reheating in magma-poor margins.

title: Numerical simulation of high-energy impact stress wave-induced fracturing in heterogeneous rocks
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Weiji Liu, Yuyao He, Xiaohua Zhu
abstract: Deep geothermal development requires overcoming hard rock drilling inefficiency. While percussive rock-breaking drilling technology shows promise, the propagation of stress waves in heterogeneous rock and its coupling with static weight on bit (WOB) remain poorly understood. This study aims to elucidate the rock fragmentation mechanism of impact stress waves and quantitatively evaluate the effects of WOB and stress waves on energy transfer and fragmentation efficiency. A 3D finite element model of the impact system was developed using the Voronoi algorithm and the Concrete Damaged Plasticity (CDP) model to investigate the role of stress waves in impact rock fragmentation. Results show impact energy is primarily consumed during rock damage, a critical energy transfer phase. As a result of rock heterogeneity, energy exhibits significant dispersion during stress wave propagation. Increasing WOB from 0 to 90 kN mitigates heterogeneity effects, reducing energy attenuation, increasing penetration depth, and creating "deeper and broader" damage zones. Energy transfer efficiency continuously increases with WOB, but the growth rate slows beyond 50 kN. At 50 kN WOB, increasing stress wave amplitude from 160 to 240 MPa also boosts efficiency, though the growth of WOB-assisted input energy slows. Mechanical specific energy (MSE) decreases with higher amplitude and WOB, but the trend moderates above 50 kN WOB. Increasing the WOB from 0 kN to 90 kN is more effective in improving the impact force and penetration depth of the teeth than increasing the stress wave amplitude under a WOB of 50 kN. These findings reveal how WOB suppresses stress wave attenuation caused by heterogeneity and clarify rock damage evolution under "stress wave-WOB" coupling, providing a theoretical basis for parameter optimization in deep hard rock impact drilling.

title: Influence of different types of nano-SiO 2 on the performance of oil well cement under HPHT CO 2 –SO 4 2- condition
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Xiyue Cui, Huijing Tan, Wei He, Yao Chen, Yuntian Zheng, Yuhao Wang
abstract: In geothermal wells, the major form of chemical corrosion is the complex interaction of sulphate and carbonate, as shown by the composition of geothermal fluids. High-alkalinity G-grade oil well cement is prone to corrosion in acidic environments, leading to a decline in mechanical properties and structural degradation. The addition of nano-SiO2 to cement can diminish the Ca/Si-ratio and permeability of the cement, thereby enhancing the resilience of the material to high temperatures and corrosion. Nano-SiO2 particles (NS) and nano-SiO2 sol (SS) are two typical types of nano-SiO2, and their impacts on the high-temperature and corrosion resistance of cement require comparison. This paper employs compressive strength experiments, XRD, FTIR, MIP, SEM, 29Si-NMR, TGA, and other analytical methods to analyse the effects of NS and SS on cement mechanical strength, the types and quantities of corrosion and hydration products, as well as microstructure, permeability, and pore-size distribution. The results indicate that NS enhanced C–S–H formation, characterised by a greater average chain length, higher degree of polymerisation, and reduced degree of ordering. NS facilitated the reduction of CH enrichment, enhanced CH orientation, and lead to a decrease in R , reduced Ca2+ content in the cement matrix and promoted C3S hydration. The incorporation of NS also inhibited the formation of hydration products with high Ca/Si ratios and corrosion products, lowered the average pore size and permeability of cement, thereby refining its internal structure. NS were beneficial to cement strength development under high-pressure and high-temperature CO2–SO4 2- composite corrosion conditions. However, the retarding effect of SS flocculation on cement hydration outweighed its promoting effect, resulting in reduced cement strength retention at high temperatures. Nonetheless, SS performed a similar function to NS in high-temperature CO2–SO4 2- composite corrosion conditions, although with slightly inferior performance.

title: Boolean-Fuzzy approaches for hydrothermal deposits models in an arid environment: A case study in Central Africa
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Ngo Nyouma Rachel, Njeudjang Kasi, Abdou Raouf, Xiaohui Lu, Hervé Gouet Daniel, Njandjock Nouck Philippe
abstract: Hydrothermal deposits are key indicators of the presence of geothermal energy and minerals of industrial interest. This study proposes an integrated Fuzzy-Boolean approach adapted to arid areas with low data density to produce a new model of hydrothermal exploration in a dry environment with low and dispersed vegetation cover, using Central Africa as a test case. To achieve this goal, hydrothermal alteration model obtained from ASTER data were combined and cross-validated with index mining obtained from geological and field data. Potential hydrothermal zones were identified, located, interpreted and spatially distributed using Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission and Reflection Radiometer (ASTER) data, natural gamma-ray spectrometry, morphological and geological data. The use of Fuzzy operators such as the algebraic sum and product with the gamma operator allowed a flexible combination of thematic layers, by managing exclusion and gradation relationships. Fuzzy logic alone has made it possible to reproduce the proposed model using explicit rules, unlike some machine learning approaches which require large training and validation datasets. Despite incomplete, imprecise or scattered information in the arid region, where geological, geomorphological and spectrometric contrasts were not always clear-cut, it simultaneously integrated these elements and offered better management of uncertainty and gradual transitions between classes (favourable and unfavourable zones). Combined with the index overlay method (IOM), it created a flexible way of visualising, in linear shapes and halos, the vast corridors of possible hydrothermal deposits. This modelling provides an important clue for identifying geothermal systems in the region, resulting in the formation of hydrothermal deposits in places where the circulation of hot fluids (associated with active tectonic structures and plutonic intrusions) favours alteration of the host rocks. Using innovative modelling approaches, the study highlights the potential of Boolean and Fuzzy logics as complementary tools in the hydrothermal field, as well as their adaptation to predictive mapping in arid environments where sparse vegetation, low spectrometric contrasts and sparse field data make the application of statistical techniques less reliable.

title: Heat source and upflow pathway in the Yangyi geothermal field, Qinghai-Xizang Plateau:insights from three-dimensional magnetotelluric imaging
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Wangqi Ren, Weiying Chen, Ping Zhao, Guoqiang Xue, Jianli Liu, Feng Luo, Tao Chen, Pengfei Lv, Yang Zhao, Kangxin Lei, Yiming He, Sheng Pan
abstract: The Yangyi geothermal field is one of the high-temperature geothermal fields located in the Xizang-Qinghai Plateau. The Yangyi geothermal power station, with an installed capacity of 16 MW, has generated 780 million kWh of electricity since its commissioning in October 2018. However, in recent years, both wellhead temperatures and production well discharge-rates have shown a noticeable decline. Before drilling new production wells, it is essential to identify the heat source and the principal fluid upflow pathway. To achieve this, data from 110 magnetotelluric (MT) sounding survey points were collected and a 3D electrical structure model was constructed through inversion analysis. The results revealed the following: (1) The heat source is a partial molten body located at a depth of 6–11 km in the southern part of Yangyi geothermal field. (2) In the west side of fault F3, a high-resistivity granite body acts as a barrier, preventing the shallow lateral migration of meteoric water from the Nyainqêntanglha Mountains. As a result, the water is forced to percolate deeper into the crust, where it is heated by surrounding rocks and converted into geothermal fluids. (3) The principal upflow pathway is located at the intersection of north-south and northeast-southwest trending faults at the Bujiemuqu valley in the study area. In contrast, the Nangzengqu and Qialagaiqu valleys are less favorable for drilling new production wells. These findings provide critical insights for guiding future geothermal exploration and development in the Yangyi geothermal field.

title: Patterns and controls of induced seismicity in geothermal reservoirs: insights from case studies and implications for hazard assessment and mitigation
description: Publication date: July 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 139 Author(s): Francesca De Santis, Emmanuelle Klein, Alain Thoraval, Julie Maury
abstract: This study reviews over 60 deep geothermal case studies to investigate the occurrence or absence of felt induced seismicity, across different reservoir types and exploitation strategies. The review highlights key patterns in seismogenic potential based on reservoir characteristics and operational methods. The potential for felt seismicity is very low for mass-balanced circulations in porous aquifers, low-to-moderate in deeper faulted or karstified sedimentary formations, while it is moderate-to-high for stimulations or circulations in fractured reservoirs and for production and reinjection operations in high-temperature geothermal fields. The presence of pre-existing faults or fractures, in a critical stress state and favorably oriented in the local stress field, constitutes an aggravating factor with respect to the seismic hazard of geothermal operations. The review further reveals that induced seismicity is poorly controlled by depth and lithology of the target formation but rather linked to rock competence and fractures characteristics.
